# sgit and Git: what only sgit does, what both do, and where Git is ahead, cli.sgit.ai

> The row-by-row comparison, checked against sgit-ai 0.26.0 and the dev builds after it. Twelve things Git has no equivalent for, each with the command and Git's nearest answer: a host that reads nothing, read keys that work from any static host, custody without access, writes without reads, one folder by byte ranges from plain storage, indexes the writer ships encrypted and signed, policy the vault carries, rewinds refused by name, a secret guard, key rotation, a computable cache, files sealed to a person. Fifteen things both have, with what differs. Where Git is ahead: line-level merge and partial commits shipped in the dev builds of 28 October; the rest of the CLI team's Git-parity roadmap is designed, with sizes in days. GitHub's features move to a future server. And the six things zero knowledge rules out, each with its substitute.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/sgit-and-git.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit and Git

**sgit is not a copy of Git with encryption on top.** It has Git's verbs, so a Git user is at home in an hour. But the host reads nothing, and that makes possible a set of things Git cannot do at all. This page is the map, row by row, checked against sgit-ai 0.26.0:
- what only sgit does;
- what both do, and how they differ;
- where Git is ahead, and how fast the gap is closing;
- what zero knowledge rules out for good.

![sgit and Git, row by row, against sgit-ai 0.26.0 and the dev builds after it. Twelve things only sgit does, from a host that reads nothing to files sealed to a person. Fifteen both do, with sgit's difference. Where Git is ahead: line-level merge and partial commits shipped in the dev builds of 28 October, seven more items designed and sized in days, GitHub's features moved to a future server. And six that zero knowledge rules out for good, each with a client-side substitute.](../articles/images/sg-map.webp)

*sgit and Git, row by row, against sgit-ai 0.26.0 and the dev builds after it. Twelve things only sgit does, from a host that reads nothing to files sealed to a person. Fifteen both do, with sgit's difference. Where Git is ahead: line-level merge and partial commits shipped in the dev builds of 28 October, seven more items designed and sized in days, GitHub's features moved to a future server. And six that zero knowledge rules out for good, each with a client-side substitute.*


**In one paragraph.** Use sgit when the files must stay unreadable to whoever stores them, when readers should need no account, or when many agents work in one large vault, one folder each. Use Git when you need blame, bisect or rebase today, a forge's review and CI, or twenty years of tooling; line-level merges and partial commits arrived in sgit's dev builds on 28 October. Almost everything on Git's side runs on the client in Git too, so sgit can build it. What sgit can never do is anything that needs the host to read your files.

The evidence:
- the sgit CLI team's [claim-by-claim review](../research/sgit-and-git-article-review.md) of the newsroom's article [What sgit does that Git does not](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/what-sgit-does-that-git-does-not.html), against the CLI's source and threat model;
- three behaviours re-run by this site against the PyPI release, [the script](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Cli/tree/dev/admin/research/sgit-and-git-2026-10-28);
- Git's and GitHub's own documentation.

## 1. What only sgit does {#only-sgit}

"No equivalent" means the mainstream Git toolchain and GitHub. Add-ons such as git-crypt and git-remote-gcrypt cover parts of the first row, with the trade-offs their own READMEs state.

| # | What sgit does | How | Git's nearest answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The host reads nothing.** Contents, file names, commit messages and branch names are encrypted on the client (AES-256-GCM) before they leave it | every command; objects stored under opaque ids | git-crypt encrypts contents only; its README says it "does not encrypt file names, commit messages" or other metadata |
| 2 | **A read key is a capability, not a permission.** It is derived one way from the vault key, so it can never become write access. It reads from any static host, with no account and no server code | [`clone --read-key`](../reference/clone.md), `--transport static`, [`sgit publish`](../reference/publish.md) | read access is a role a server enforces (a collaborator, a deploy key), or the repository is public |
| 3 | **Custody without access.** Copy a published vault you cannot read, keyless, and verify it. A backup service or a second host holds and checks the vault and learns nothing | [`sgit vault mirror`](../reference/vault.md) `[--verify DIR]` | a mirror of a Git repository can read all of it |
| 4 | **Write without read.** An append lane lets a sender put something into a vault and learn nothing, not even whether anyone else writes there: the answer is `{"ok": true}` | the server's [append lanes](../api/append-lanes.md); **no sgit command yet** | no Git or GitHub role can write without reading |
| 5 | **One folder by byte ranges from plain storage.** A scoped clone of a pack vault reads the packs' directories, then only that folder's byte ranges, verifying each object by its hash. On 76,000 files: 2.8 s and 12.5 MB, against 36 s and the whole 88 MB pack | [`clone --path`](../reference/clone.md) on a pack vault (0.26.0) | Git's dumb HTTP takes whole packs; its partial clone needs a smart server that reads the content |
| 6 | **Indexes the writer ships, encrypted and signed.** Each push carries an index pack beside its data pack, so readers plan pulls and clones without walking trees. An index is a plan, never a proof: every object is still verified by its id | automatic on pack vaults (0.26.0); [`pack index build \| verify \| stats`](../reference/pack.md) | Git's commit-graph and pack indexes are built by each reader, as local plaintext caches |
| 7 | **Policy carried by the vault.** The format gate (`min_client`, features) and `signatures-required` live in the encrypted branch index. Every sgit client enforces them before it writes anything | [`sgit vault format`](../reference/vault.md) (0.19.0) | signature checks are each user's local config; a repository cannot require them of whoever clones it |
| 8 | **A rewind is refused by name, on every clone.** A remote head that does not descend from the last one this clone accepted is refused, even though the host took the forced push (it cannot read refs) | `pull` refuses; `pull --accept-rewind` takes it (0.19.0) | the default `+` refspec takes a forced update with one line of output; `receive.denyNonFastForwards` is a server setting |
| 9 | **A secret guard at commit.** A vault key in a zip under any name, a hard link to one of the clone's secrets, and `.env` files are refused | `commit`, `write` | nothing built in; GitHub's push protection runs on a server that reads the content |
| 10 | **Rotate the key that encrypts the history.** Move a vault to a new key, and optionally a new server | [`sgit vault rekey`](../reference/vault.md), `vault move` | a leaked credential is revoked on the server; the content was never encrypted |
| 11 | **A computable cache.** A hot path gets a fixed-cost read at a location only key holders can compute, so an edge function reads it in one request, without walking trees | [`sgit cache add`](../reference/cache.md) | every read walks from a ref |
| 12 | **Seal a file to a person.** Encrypt a file to someone's public key, then commit the sealed file | [`sgit pki encrypt --recipient`](../reference/pki.md) | Git signs commits; it has no "encrypt this to that person" |

Checked by this site against 0.26.0: rows 8 and 9, and `write` in section 2 ([the script and its output](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Cli/tree/dev/admin/research/sgit-and-git-2026-10-28)). The other rows are from the CLI team's review of the code, and from the release notes of [0.24.0](../docs/update-to-0-24-0.md), [0.25.0](../docs/update-to-0-25-0.md) and [0.26.0](../docs/update-to-0-26-0.md).

## 2. What both have, and what differs {#both}

| Git | sgit | What differs |
|---|---|---|
| packs | pack mode (0.24.0) | sgit's packs are ciphertext on plain object storage; Git's are delta-compressed, sgit's are not |
| kept packs above `fetch.unpackLimit` | `clone --pack-store` (0.26.0) | the same idea; sgit verifies each object on every read |
| partial clone plus sparse-checkout | `clone --path`, `fetch <folder>` to widen, `clone --sparse` (0.18.0) | against ciphertext on S3. A commit outside the scope is refused by name, and two scoped clones in different folders never conflict |
| `clone --no-checkout` | `clone --no-checkout`, then `sgit checkout <paths>` (0.26.0) | the agent loop: `pull --no-checkout`, then `checkout --since-pull` writes only what changed |
| shallow clone, `fetch --unshallow` | `clone --depth N`, `fetch --unshallow` (0.18.0) | combines with `--path` |
| bare clone | `clone --bare`, `clone-headless`, `clone-branch`, `clone-range` | |
| `git commit <paths>`, `add -p` | `sgit commit <paths>`, `commit -p`, `--list-hunks` / `--hunk` (0.26.6); `sgit write <path> --file F [--also P:F …] [--push] [--json]` | `commit <paths>` matches Git's committed trees; hunk ids refuse to pick a different hunk once the file changed; `write` commits files without scanning the working copy. No persistent staging area |
| signed commits and tags | commits signed by each clone's key; verification and `signatures-required` (0.19.0); signed tags (0.21.0) | sgit's check is required by the vault (row 7). A signature proves a key holder, not a person; see [section 5](#qualifiers) |
| `log`, `diff`, `show`, `reflog` | `history log --grep --since --until --author --file --patch --stat --json`, `history diff A..B`, `history show`, `history reflog` | `history log --vault-key` runs with no clone |
| `revert`, `reset`, `commit --amend` | `history revert`, `history reset`, `history undo`, `commit --amend` (0.21.0) | |
| `stash` | `vault stash` | |
| `merge` and conflicts | `branch merge`, `resolve`, `merge-abort` | whole-file `<path>.conflict` by default; line-level with Git's markers with `--merge lines` (0.26.5) |
| `remote` | `remote add / list / set-url` | |
| `fsck` | `check fsck`, `check verify` | checks encrypted objects and their signatures; can repair |
| reading over dumb HTTP | `--transport static` | one file from a normal vault is a ref, a commit, one tree per folder level and the blob, as plain GETs; one batch request for a path declared with `sgit cache add` |

The full Git-to-sgit command table is [sgit for Git users](../docs/sgit-for-git-users.md).

## 3. Where Git is ahead, and how fast the gap is closing {#git-ahead}

Git is a client-side program. Almost all of its lead runs on the client in Git too, on plaintext the client holds, so sgit can build the same things with no new server feature.
- **The plan:** the CLI team's [Git-parity roadmap](../research/git-parity-roadmap.md) (28 October): Git the client is the bar, and every new feature is off by default.
- **The first deliveries** are already on PyPI as [dev builds](../builds/index.md), each reviewed.
- **Sizes** are the roadmap's estimates.

```text
 Git's lead on 27 Oct            on 28 Oct, dev builds 0.26.3 – 0.26.6
 ──────────────────────          ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 line-level merge         ──►    ✓ shipped, opt-in: pull/branch merge --merge lines   0.26.5
 commit some files/hunks  ──►    ✓ shipped: commit <paths>, -p, --list-hunks/--hunk    0.26.6
 commit messages > 740 B  ──►    ✓ shipped: up to 64 KiB with long-messages            0.26.4
 forks deeper than 200    ──►    ✓ fixed: merge base with no cap                        0.26.3
 the rest of priority 1-2 ──►    designed, with acceptance checklists: 7 documents
```

| Git has | sgit, 28 October | Roadmap | Design | Size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| line-by-line three-way merge | **shipped, opt-in** in [0.26.5](../builds/0-26-5.md): `--merge lines`, `--conflict diff3`; whole-file `.conflict` stays the default | 2.1 | [01](../research/git-parity-design-line-merge.md) | done |
| a staging area, `commit <paths>`, `commit -p` | **shipped** in [0.26.6](../builds/0-26-6.md): `commit <paths>`, `commit -p`, and `--list-hunks` / `--hunk` for agents; no persistent `add` | 2.3 | [03](../research/git-parity-design-partial-commits.md) | done |
| sign with your own key, verify against your allowed signers | each clone signs with its own key; designed: an SSH or GPG key as a second signature, and an allowed-signers file per verifier, as Git does | 2.2 | [02](../research/git-parity-design-signing.md) | 3–4 days |
| `cherry-pick` | designed, on the line merge | 2.8 | [01](../research/git-parity-design-line-merge.md) | 1 day |
| rename detection | none; designed from the plaintext content hash tree entries already carry | 2.4 | [04](../research/git-parity-design-blame-grep.md) | 1–2 days |
| `blame` | none; designed as `history blame`, cheap through the index pack's file → commits member | 2.5 | [04](../research/git-parity-design-blame-grep.md) | 2 days |
| `grep`, `log -S` / `-G` | `history log --grep` over messages; designed: `sgit grep` over content | 2.7 | [04](../research/git-parity-design-blame-grep.md) | 1–2 days |
| `bisect` | none; designed, by generation number | 2.6 | [05](../research/git-parity-design-bisect.md) | 1–2 days |
| hooks | none; designed as local hooks that never sync | 2.9 | [03](../research/git-parity-design-partial-commits.md) | 1 day |
| `rebase`, `pull --rebase`, `rebase -i` | none; designed, opt-in, never rewriting pushed history | 2.12 | [07](../research/git-parity-design-rebase.md) | 2–3 days |
| `worktree` | none; designed: a second working copy in seconds that borrows the main store, like Git's alternates | 2.13 | [06](../research/git-parity-design-worktree.md) | 2–3 days |
| garbage collection | none; compaction moves old packs to `archive/`; client-driven `vault prune` planned | 2.10 | | 2–3 days |
| delta compression | each blob deflated, no deltas; needs a format feature and a gate | 2.11 | | 1–2 weeks |
| `archive`, `shortlog`, `describe`, aliases | none | 2.14 | | small each |
| read one file with no clone, from the CLI | the browser reader does it on normal vaults; on pack vaults, Phase 4 of [pack indexes](../dev/pack-indexes/index.md) | | | S / L |
| a command for append lanes | the server feature only | | | S–M |
| per-folder read access | one key per vault; a scoped clone is not a boundary; would need folder keys | | | XL |
| submodules | none; a design if someone asks | 2.15 | | design |
| 160-bit ids by default | format 2, 128-bit, opt-in since 0.19.0 | | | shipped, opt-in |
| twenty years of maturity | a month of releases, now one reviewed build per merge | | | time |

**Moved to a future server, "SGitHub"** ([the roadmap, section 4](../research/git-parity-roadmap.md)): GitHub's features, not Git's.
- accounts, and who pushed;
- branches protected per person;
- an owner-signed list of who may write, which closes TM-R01;
- review, CI and verified badges.

These are possible under zero knowledge, with per-member write tokens checked by ref id and review objects kept in the vault, but they belong to a host, not to the CLI.

## 4. What zero knowledge rules out {#ruled-out}

These are limits of the model, not of effort. Each has a substitute on the client.

| Ruled out | Why | The substitute |
|---|---|---|
| anything the host must read to do: server-side search, diffs, a merge button, code scanning, language statistics | the host holds ciphertext; giving it the key ends zero knowledge | do it in the client, the browser, or a runner the key holder controls |
| taking back what a reader already has | no system can; a removed GitHub collaborator keeps their clone too | rotate forward (`vault rekey`, `vault move`), delete the old vault; per-folder keys limit what each reader ever got |
| per-folder permissions inside one key | the host cannot tell folders apart, and the key decrypts every object | per-folder keys (section 3) |
| hiding all metadata | sizes, timing, counts and access patterns are visible to any store | padding, fixed-size packs and decoy reads reduce it at a bandwidth cost; only an ORAM-style protocol removes it |
| the host optimising the store: repacking, deltas, dedupe across vaults | the host has only ciphertext; dedupe across vaults would need convergent encryption, which leaks equality | client-side deltas and prune (section 3) |
| a host that enforces fast-forward-only | the host cannot read a ref, so it cannot check ancestry | the client-side rewind guard (row 8), shipped |

## 5. The qualifiers {#qualifiers}

Said plainly, so that nobody builds on a stronger claim than the code makes:

- **What the host still sees:**
  - sizes, timing and object counts;
  - in pack mode, which commit each push carried;
  - which trees are equal, because tree encryption is deterministic;
  - with `blob-deflate`, how compressible each file is;
  - the sizes of index packs;
  - in path-ordered packs, which blobs share a folder;
  - for a scoped clone, which byte ranges it read.
- **Reading is a capability; writing is a permission.** The write key is a bearer secret that the host checks, with no cryptographic role. A read-key holder who can write to the store can author history that `check verify` calls verified. A signature today proves "a key holder", not a particular clone or person. This is the threat model's top accepted risk, TM-R01. On the roadmap, own-key signing (design 02) lets each verifier decide whom to trust, as Git does, and an owner-signed list of who may write moves to the future server.
- **An index is checked under the vault's signature policy.** An unsigned index is accepted unless the vault has `signatures-required`. A signing teammate could mislead a fresh clone's working copy, as a commit from that key could. `sgit pack index verify` catches it (TM-R42).
- **A read key cannot be revoked after the fact,** and it is per vault, not per folder (TM-R12). The remedy is rotation, as above.

*Sources: the CLI team's [review of the newsroom's article](../research/sgit-and-git-article-review.md), written against SGit-AI__CLI at `640069a`; sgit-ai 0.26.0 from PyPI and its [command reference](../reference/index.md); [the check script](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Cli/tree/dev/admin/research/sgit-and-git-2026-10-28), run on 28 October 2026; [git-crypt's README](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt/blob/master/README.md); Git's documentation on [git-clone](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone) and [git-config](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config). Where this page and the code disagree, the code wins and this page is wrong: say so on [GitHub](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/issues).*

# sgit for git users, cli.sgit.ai

> The Rosetta stone: every git command mapped to its sgit equivalent, plus the three deliberate differences.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/sgit-for-git-users.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/sgit-for-git-users.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

# sgit for git users

If you know git, you know most of sgit. Same verbs, same mental model, with three deliberate differences that exist because the payload is encrypted.

> **Updated, 28 October 2026, against sgit-ai 0.26.0.** sgit is not only Git with encryption: it does twelve things Git has no equivalent for, and Git is still ahead on sixteen. The map is [sgit and Git](../docs/sgit-and-git.md). Rows below gained `write`, the clone options and `checkout`.

## The Rosetta stone

| git | sgit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `git init` | `sgit init` | `--existing` vault-ifies a non-empty folder |
| `git clone <url>` | `sgit clone <vault-key>` | the key is URL + auth + decryption in one |
| `git status` | `sgit status` | `--explain` teaches the branch model |
| `git commit -am` | `sgit commit -m` | the whole folder. There is no staging area |
| `git commit <paths>` | `sgit write <path> --file F --also P:F` | whole files, committed atomically to HEAD; other edits stay uncommitted; `--push --json` for agents |
| `git clone --filter` + sparse-checkout | `sgit clone --path FOLDER`, `sgit fetch FOLDER` | a commit outside the scope is refused by name |
| `git clone --depth` / `fetch --unshallow` | `sgit clone --depth N` / `sgit fetch --unshallow` | |
| `git clone --no-checkout` + `git checkout -- <paths>` | `sgit clone --no-checkout` + `sgit checkout <paths>` | `pull --no-checkout`, then `checkout --since-pull` writes only what changed |
| `git tag -s` | `sgit vault tag` | signed |
| `git push / pull / fetch` | `sgit push / pull / fetch` | push is delta + ciphertext only |
| `git log` | `sgit history log` | `--oneline`, `--patch`, `--json`, ranges |
| `git diff` | `sgit history diff` | `--remote`, `--commit`, `--files-only` |
| `git show` | `sgit history show` | read-only, fetches missing objects without merging |
| `git revert / reset` | `sgit history revert / reset` |  |
| `git stash` | `sgit vault stash` | `pop`, `list`, `drop` |
| `git branch / checkout` | `sgit branch new / switch / checkout` |  |
| `git merge` conflicts | `sgit resolve --show` | three-way base/ours/theirs view with a verdict per file |
| `git remote` | `sgit remote add / list / set-url` |  |
| `git fsck` | `sgit check fsck` | verifies encrypted object integrity, can repair |

## The three differences that matter

### 1. No staging area

`sgit commit` snapshots the whole folder. This removes git's most confusing concept. To commit some files and not others, `sgit write` commits the named files whole and leaves the rest uncommitted. What does not exist is choosing hunks within a file.

### 2. The vault key is URL, auth, and encryption key in one

`passphrase:vault-id`. There is no separate remote URL to configure, no separate credential to manage, and no password reset. Whoever holds the key holds the vault, treat it like the private key it is.

### 3. Two layers of branches

You never work directly on a shared branch. Every clone works on a private **clone branch** (its key never leaves your machine) and `push` forwards commits to the shared **named branch**. That's why two agents on the same vault can't corrupt each other's work-in-progress. [The full story →](../docs/two-branch-model.md)

# The two-branch model, cli.sgit.ai

> sgit's central idea: private clone branches per machine or agent, shared named branches, and explicit publishing.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/two-branch-model.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/two-branch-model.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# The two-branch model

sgit's central architectural idea: every clone works on a private branch, and sharing is an explicit act.

## Clone branches and named branches

```
        agent A's machine                    the server                    agent B's machine
  ┌───────────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────────┐
  │  clone branch (A)     │  push  │   named branch "main"     │  pull  │  clone branch (B)     │
  │  key: local only ─────┼───────▶│   key: shared via vault   │◀───────┼─ key: local only      │
  └───────────────────────┘        └───────────────────────────┘        └───────────────────────┘
```

- **Named branches** (`main`, `feature-x`, …) are shared and live on the server, encrypted, like everything else.
- **Clone branches** are created per clone. Their key is stored only in `.sg_vault/local/` and is never pushed. All your commits land here first.
- `sgit push` re-encrypts your clone-branch commits with the named branch's key and forwards them. `sgit pull` brings named-branch commits down and merges them into your clone branch.

Run `sgit status --explain` any time, it prints this model with your vault's actual branch names filled in.

## Why it works this way

- **Isolation by construction.** Two machines, or two agents, on the same vault physically cannot overwrite each other's uncommitted or unpushed work: they're on different branches with different keys.
- **Sharing is explicit.** Nothing you commit is visible to anyone until you `push`. An agent can iterate messily in private and publish only the result.
- **Safe concurrent pushes.** Pushes use compare-and-swap on the server (atomic batch writes): if someone pushed before you, your push is rejected cleanly instead of silently clobbering, pull, merge, push again.

## Merging and conflicts

When histories diverge, sgit runs a genuine three-way merge (common ancestor + ours + theirs) per file. Non-conflicting changes merge automatically; conflicting paths get `.conflict` files, and:

```
$ sgit resolve --show
  notes/plan.md   CONFLICT (both changed)
    base   │ ship in Q3
    ours   │ ship in Q4          ← your clone branch
    theirs │ ship in Q3, beta Q2 ← the named branch
    verdict: genuine conflict  (not one-sided, not identical)
```

The verdict line matters in multi-writer vaults: it distinguishes genuine conflicts from one-sided or identical changes, so you (or an agent) only spend attention where a human decision is actually required. `sgit merge-abort` backs out of a merge cleanly.

# Update sgit-ai to 0.18.0

A short page for an agent, or a person running agents, that has been told "read this and update". Five minutes. sgit-ai 0.18.0 was published to PyPI on 7 October 2026.

**The current release is 0.21.0.** `sgit update` takes you straight there. This page is still the one to read for the clone command (`--path`, `--depth`); for everything since, read [Update sgit-ai to 0.21.0](../docs/update-to-0-21-0.md).

## 1. Update and check

```
$ sgit update          # wraps: pip install --upgrade sgit-ai
$ sgit version
sgit-ai v0.18.0
```

If `sgit version` still shows 0.16.x or 0.17.0, you have more than one Python environment; run `python -m pip install --upgrade sgit-ai` in the one your harness uses, then check again. [Installation](../docs/installation.md) has the rest.

## 2. What changes for you

| Before | Now | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| A full clone of a large shared vault took minutes and sometimes hit your command timeout | A scoped clone of your folder takes seconds; a full clone is about twice as fast | Clone with `--path <your-folder> --depth 1` (below) |
| `sgit pull`, and the pull inside `sgit push`, could silently revert a file you had edited but not committed | Your edit is kept, or the pull is refused before anything is written and tells you which file | When you see `error: your local changes would be overwritten by pull`, run `sgit commit`, then push again. It is a normal outcome, not a failure |
| `sgit status` could say your fresh clone was "200 ahead" | It says how many commits the remote really has that you do not (`50+` means at least 50) | Trust it |
| A file created and changed again before one push left its first version missing on the server | Every pushed commit's files are uploaded | If you have an old clone that pushed such commits, run `sgit check upload-objects` in it once |
| `sgit clone-branch`, `clone-headless` and `clone-range` failed with `Name or service not known` | They work | Nothing; prefer `sgit clone --depth 1` over `clone-branch` |

## 3. Change your clone command

Old:

```
$ sgit clone <vault-key> workspace
```

New, if you work inside one folder, which most agents do:

```
$ sgit clone --path mail/<your-account> --depth 1 <vault-key> workspace
```

- `--path <folder-name>` holds only that folder (repeat it for several). Everything else in the vault is carried by id: your commits and pushes are exactly what a full clone would produce, and nothing another agent does in another folder can conflict with yours.
- `--depth 1` holds the newest commit only. Commit, push, pull and status work normally; history stops there.
- Need another folder later: `sgit fetch <folder-name>`. Need the history: `sgit fetch --unshallow`.
- Writes outside your held folders are refused and name the file. That is the scope working, not a bug: widen, or use a full clone for that change.
- `sgit check fsck`, `sgit dev dump`, `sgit publish` and `sgit vault move` need a full clone.

On a vault of about 600 commits and 9,400 files, measured by the CLI team from a cloud sandbox: full clone 80 s and 173 MB, one folder of 365 files 14 s and 3.2 MB, two small folders 5 s.

## 4. Change nothing else

`commit`, `push`, `pull`, `status`, `cat`, `ls` and `write` are the same commands with the same output, except that `status` is now right and `pull` protects your uncommitted work. A full clone without `--path` or `--depth` behaves exactly as before, only faster.

## 5. If you want the detail

- [sgit-ai 0.18.0, the release notes](https://sgit.ai/updates/index.html#sgit-ai-0-18-0): everything that changed, with the measurements.
- [Partial clones](../docs/partial-clones.md): `--path`, `--depth`, widening, limits.
- [Agents sharing one vault](../docs/agents-sharing-one-vault.md): the recommended loop and the full table of what a pull does with uncommitted work.

# Update sgit-ai to 0.21.0, cli.sgit.ai

> For an agent team: sgit update, what now refuses and what to do (symlinks, unreadable files, SGIT_DEFAULT_BASE_URL, key zips, branch names, rewinds, signatures), the new history commands (undo, reflog, amend, revert --as-commit, shorthand, log filters), signed tags, --force-with-lease, notes for vault owners and mixed 0.20/0.21 teams. Covers 0.19.0 and 0.20.0. Published 11 October 2026.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-21-0.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-21-0.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

# Update sgit-ai to 0.21.0

A page for an agent, or a person running agents, that has been told "read this and update". Ten minutes. sgit-ai 0.21.0 was published to PyPI on 10 October 2026. It includes everything in 0.19.0 and 0.20.0, so coming from 0.18.0 or older this is the only page you need. **Your daily loop does not change**: `pull`, work, `commit`, `push`. What changes is what sgit now refuses to do, and a set of history commands you have been missing.

## 1. Update and check

```
$ sgit update          # wraps: pip install --upgrade sgit-ai
$ sgit version
sgit-ai v0.21.0
```

If `sgit version` still shows an older number, you have more than one Python environment; run `python -m pip install --upgrade sgit-ai` in the one your harness uses, then check again. [Installation](../docs/installation.md) has the rest. Your existing clones need nothing: the first command in each one records the server it uses and moves its bookkeeping to the 0.21.0 layout.

## 2. What now refuses, and what to do

0.21.0 is a security release. Each of these used to work, or work silently and do damage. Each refusal names the file or branch and says what to do; none changes anything before it stops.

| You see | Why | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `warning: skipped symlink <path>` on commit | sgit never stores, follows or writes through a link. A link to `.sg_vault/local/vault_key` used to commit the vault key itself | Nothing. Commit the real file if you meant to. A tracked file replaced by a link keeps its committed version; `status` and `pull` name it |
| `cannot read <file> (Permission denied); nothing was changed` | A file sgit cannot open used to read as deleted, and a commit removed it for everyone | Close the program holding it or fix its permissions, then run the command again |
| a refusal naming `SGIT_DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | The variable used to silently redirect a vault, with your token and write key, to whatever host it named | Name the server once: `sgit --base-url <url> <command>` (the flag goes before a group too), or `sgit remote add origin <url>`. Vaults made by 0.21.0 already record it |
| a commit refused over a zip that holds a key | A backup zip (or any zip) holding a vault key or a private signing key would hand it to every reader | Delete it, or move it out of the vault folder. `sgit commit --allow-secret-file <path>` commits one on purpose |
| `a branch named '<name>' already exists on the server` on push | A teammate pushed a branch with that name first; yours used to land where nobody could see it | `sgit branch rename <name> <new-name>`, then `sgit push` |
| `the named branch was REWOUND`; `push` exits 1 | Someone force-pushed, or the server served an old pointer | Do not accept it on your own; tell the vault owner. If it was deliberate: `sgit pull --accept-rewind`, which keeps your own unpushed commits and drops the removed ones |
| `this vault needs sgit-ai >= X.Y.Z` | The owner raised the vault's minimum client | `sgit update`, then retry |
| a pull, clone or push refused over an unsigned commit | The vault requires signed commits (`signatures-required`) | Tell the vault owner. If your clone has no signing key (it says `UNSIGNED` when you commit), clone the vault again |
| `'abcdef1' is not a valid tag name`, or a revision refused as ambiguous | A tag named like a commit id would shadow it | Pick another name. For an existing short-hex tag write `tag:<name>`, or the full commit id |
| `sgit: 'log' is now sgit history log` (exit 2) | Commands moved into groups in earlier releases | Use the name it prints |

## 3. New commands worth knowing

All local, all safe to try. Every example below is output from 0.21.0 on the live dev server, 11 October 2026.

### History, the way git users expect it

```
$ sgit history log --grep more --stat
  f7a8b9646ae9 (HEAD)  add more  ~1  [blobs:+1]
      M  notes.md

$ sgit history show HEAD~1
commit obj-cas-imm-bb27e943d81d
parent obj-cas-imm-326e87100964
    first notes
+ notes.md  (8 bytes)
```

- **Revisions everywhere a commit is named:** `HEAD`, `@`, `HEAD~2`, `HEAD^2`, `@{1}` (where this clone's head was), tag names, the 12-hex id `history log` prints, or any unique prefix of 4+ characters.
- **Log filters:** `--grep`, `--since` / `--until` (`2026-10-08`, `3d`, `"2 weeks ago"`, `yesterday`), `--author` (a signing key id or branch name), `--stat`. They follow merged-in commits too.

### Undo, amend, revert

```
$ sgit history undo
Undone: this clone's head is back at f7a8b9646ae9 (was d9c5d05ea052).
  1 file(s) restored, 0 removed. Run it again to redo; sgit history reflog shows every move.

$ sgit history reflog -n 3
  @{0}  f7a8b9646ae9  2026-10-11 15:54:26  add more  (was d9c5d05ea052)
  @{1}  d9c5d05ea052  2026-10-11 15:54:25  local mistake  (was f7a8b9646ae9)
  @{2}  f7a8b9646ae9  2026-10-11 15:54:09  add more  (was bb27e943d81d)
```

| Command | What it does | When |
|---|---|---|
| `sgit history undo` | moves this clone's head back to before its last move, restoring the files; run again to redo | a local commit you regret, before pushing |
| `sgit history reflog` | every move of this clone's head (local, last 1,000); `sgit history reset <id>` brings one back | after a reset, an accepted rewind or a bad merge |
| `sgit commit --amend [-m …]` | replaces the last commit; refused once it is on the server | a typo in the message, a forgotten file |
| `sgit history revert --as-commit --commit <rev>` | a new, signed commit that inverts an earlier one (git's `revert`) | undoing a **pushed** change for everyone |

Plain `sgit history revert` still restores files without committing, as before.

### Tags, branches, safer force

```
$ sgit vault tag create v1.0 -m "first release"
Tagged f7a8b9646ae9 as v1.0, signed by this clone.
$ sgit vault tag list
  ✓ v1.0  f7a8b9646ae9  2026-10-11 15:54 UTC  first release
```

- **Signed tags** (`sgit vault tag create | list | show | delete`): an encrypted, signed object; the name lives only in the encrypted branch index, so the server never sees it. Tags do not move without `--force`, and a pull reports a tag that moved. A tag name works wherever a commit does.
- **Branches work end to end:** `branch new`, `branch switch` (fetches first), `branch merge <name>`, and `branch rename` for a branch not yet pushed. Before 0.21.0, work on a branch was pushed to the main branch.
- **`sgit push --force-with-lease`**: forces only if the remote is still where this clone last accepted it, and writes with compare-and-swap, so a teammate's push is never clobbered. Running `status` in between does not satisfy the lease.
- **`sgit doctor`** names the server it checks and sends the same headers as push and pull; `sgit clone - <dir>` reads the vault key from stdin, so it never appears in your command line or shell history.

## 4. If you are the vault owner

Nothing changes for a vault until you raise it. 0.21.0 is the first release where the history-integrity features are safe for a team of writers.

```
$ sgit vault format --set 2 --min-client 0.21.0 --feature signatures-required
Vault format updated and written to the server.
  …
  Format:      2  (new objects get 32-hex ids)
  Min client:  0.21.0   (this client: v0.21.0)
  Features:    ids-128, signatures-required, signed-since-82bcf306a04a
```

- **`--min-client 0.21.0`** is the recommended floor: a 0.19.0 or 0.20.0 client is then refused by name (`this vault needs sgit-ai >= 0.21.0 and this is 0.20.0: run `sgit update``, checked on 11 October). It also keeps 0.20.0 clients from dropping the vault's tags, below.
- **`signatures-required`** now works with several writers. Clone, pull and push all check it. Only commits after the moment you switch it on (`signed-since-…`) must be signed, so older unsigned history is fine.
- **Clients older than 0.19.0 do not know the gate exists.** On a raised vault they fail and blame the data ("integrity check refused vault data", "missing file … sgit check fsck"). The fix for them is `sgit update`, never `vault move` or `fsck --repair`. Raise a vault only when every writer is on 0.21.0.

The whole model (the gate, 128-bit ids, rewinds, signatures) is in [History integrity](../docs/history-integrity.md).

## 5. Mixed teams: 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 on one vault

Clone, pull, commit and push work in both directions, and every commit verifies (checked live on 10 and 11 October). Two things to know:

- **Tags disappear while a 0.20.0 client is active.** The first push of a 0.20.0 clone leaves the server with no tags; a 0.21.0 clone that still holds them restores them on its next pull, but a fresh clone made in between sees none. For a vault that uses tags: `--min-client 0.21.0`.
- **A 0.20.0 backup has no signing key.** A clone restored from it makes unsigned commits (it warns `UNSIGNED`); under `signatures-required` it cannot push until it is cloned again. 0.21.0 backups carry the key.

**If anyone on your team is still on 0.20.0 or older:** after `sgit vault uninit`, delete the `*__uninit.zip` it leaves in the folder before the next `sgit commit`. On those versions the zip, which holds the vault key, is committed like any other file. 0.21.0 names it so it is never committed, and refuses any zip holding a key.

## 6. If you want the detail

- [sgit-ai 0.21.0, the release notes](https://sgit.ai/updates/index.html#sgit-ai-0-21-0): what changed since 0.18.0, and how it was checked.
- [History integrity](../docs/history-integrity.md): the format gate, signatures, rewinds and the checklist for raising a vault.
- [Agents sharing one vault](../docs/agents-sharing-one-vault.md): the recommended loop for a team.
- The CLI's full change log, with every fix: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

# sgit-ai 0.24.0 release notes: pack mode, cli.sgit.ai

> Release notes for sgit-ai 0.24.0, for people and agents. Pack mode is new and opt-in: a vault whose objects travel as zips, cloned in a handful of requests whatever its history, with files compressed before they are encrypted. The commands (init --packs, pack import, export, compact, ls, stats, verify), what was measured, the gate that refuses older clients by name, what does not work on a pack vault yet, the two transport changes every vault gets, and how the release was reviewed. Normal vaults behave as before.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-24-0.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit-ai 0.24.0: pack mode

The release notes for 0.24.0, written to be read by a person or handed to an agent. **If you do nothing, nothing changes**: existing vaults stay normal vaults, and your daily loop (`pull`, work, `commit`, `push`) is the same. What is new is a second kind of vault, a **pack vault**, which you opt into for a new vault or by converting a copy of an existing one. To start using it, see [Pack mode: a playbook for agents](../docs/pack-mode-for-agents.md).

## 1. Update and check

```text
$ sgit update          # wraps: pip install --upgrade sgit-ai
$ sgit version
sgit-ai v0.24.0
$ sgit pack --help     # lists import, export, compact, ls, verify, stats
```

If `sgit version` shows an older number, you have more than one Python environment. Run `python -m pip install --upgrade sgit-ai` in the one your harness uses. Existing clones need nothing.

## 2. What is new: pack vaults

A normal vault stores every object as its own file on the host, so a clone of a long history is thousands of requests. A pack vault stores them as zips:

- **Every push uploads one zip** holding the commit's new objects. The ref then moves under compare-and-swap, exactly as before.
- **The first push, and each compaction, uploads one snapshot zip** holding the whole history.
- **A clone takes the snapshot for the branch head plus the commit zips since it.** That is three or four requests, whatever the size of the history.
- **A pull that is N pushes behind** is two listings and one batch of N zips.

**Files are compressed before they are encrypted**, so a text-heavy vault holds about half the bytes on the host. The server is unchanged: pack mode uses the batch, presigned, list and delete routes it already had.

The local store stays one file per object. Packs are unpacked on arrival, each object checked against its content address before it is written. So every local command (`history log`, `cat`, `diff`, `branch`, `stash`, `vault tag`) works exactly as on a normal vault.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sgit init --packs [dir]`, `sgit create --packs <name>` | A new pack vault. |
| `sgit pack import <normal clone> <new dir>` | Rewrites a **full** clone of a normal vault into a **new** pack vault with its own key. The commits keep their messages and timestamps and are re-signed by the new clone. The source is untouched. The new vault's first `sgit push` uploads one snapshot. `--no-deflate` keeps file contents uncompressed; `--json` prints the stats. |
| `sgit pack export <pack clone> <new dir>` | The reverse: a **new** normal vault, nothing packed, nothing compressed. |
| `sgit pack compact [dir] [--dry-run]` | One snapshot of the current head. The packs it absorbs, the snapshots it supersedes and orphan packs older than a day move to `bare/packs/archive/`. Each is copied, the copy confirmed by listing, and only then the original deleted; `archive/` is never deleted. |
| `sgit pack ls`, `sgit pack stats`, `sgit pack verify` | What the host holds, folder by folder; packs and bytes plus the local compression ratio; every member of every pack checked against its content address. All three take `--json`. |
| `push`, `pull`, `clone`, `status` | Unchanged to use. On a pack vault they move packs. |

On the host, a pack vault looks like this:

```text
bare/packs/commits/    <epoch>__<commit id>__<bytes>.zip    one per push
bare/packs/snapshots/  <epoch>__<commit id>__<bytes>.zip    the first push and each compaction
bare/packs/archive/    the same names, moved there by compaction; never deleted
bare/refs/, bare/indexes/, bare/keys/                       exactly as on a normal vault
bare/data/                                                  empty, except tag objects
```

## 3. What it measured

Each pair is the same content as a normal vault and as a pack vault, on the same server (`dev.send.sgraph.ai`), from a cloud sandbox. Medians of three runs unless one number is given.

| | Normal vault | Pack vault |
|---|---|---|
| **A published vault:** 17 commits, 699 files, 2,087 objects (the [AIUC-1 conformance vault](https://sgit.ai/demos/vaults/index.html)) | | |
| Clone | 28.6 s | **8.1 s**, 4 requests |
| First push | 27.3 s | **11.8 s** |
| Push of one file | 10.5 s | **5.8 s** |
| Pull, 3 pushes behind | 4.8 s | 4.2 s |
| Stored file contents | 213 MB | **129 MB** (1.66×) |
| **A synthetic vault:** 30 commits, 300 prose and JSON files | | |
| Clone | 5.5 s | **3.3 s**, 3 requests |
| Push of one commit | 7.3 s | **5.3 s** |
| Pull, 5 pushes behind | 5.9 s | **3.6 s** |
| Stored file contents | 1.0 MB | **0.3 MB** (3.67×) |
| **The comms vault's history:** 1,229 commits, 33,000 objects, measured by the CLI team | | |
| Full clone | 3½ min | **25 s** (18 s of it one 251 MB download in 4 requests) |

Re-measured with the 0.24.0 wheel from PyPI after the release, on 22 October: the published vault cloned in 9.0, 9.3 and 9.8 seconds (7.2 s of each was the download, in 4 requests), and imported in about 9 seconds locally. That is within the spread between runs on the same day; the network accounts for it, not the code.

Two things the table does not show:
- **Pulls gain least.** Their time is the local merge and status walks, which are the same in both modes and are the CLI team's next target.
- **After a compaction, a clone that was behind downloads the whole snapshot** on its next pull: 130 MB and 9.5 s on the AIUC vault. Archived commit packs are never read by a pull.

## 4. Compatibility

- **Older clients are refused by name.** A pack vault's index carries `min_client = 0.24.0`. Checked live: sgit-ai 0.23.0 from PyPI says `this vault needs sgit-ai >= 0.24.0 and this is 0.23.0: run sgit update, then try again`. Clients older than 0.18.1 do not read `min_client` at all and would see an empty vault; that was already the case for any gated vault.
- **No web view.** The browser does not read packs. A vault that must be browsable on vault.sgraph.ai stays a normal vault, or comes back as one through `sgit pack export`.
- **`sgit clone` works in every form** (full, `--path`, `--depth`, read-only), but `--path` and `--depth` take the packs whole in this version. A scoped clone of one folder of a big pack vault is therefore a full download.
- **`sgit clone-headless` works:** its `fetch` takes the packs. `sgit clone-branch` and `sgit clone-range` refuse a pack vault with a sentence that says so.
- **Tags work.** Tag objects are the one thing still written loose to `bare/data/`; `pack stats` counts them separately.

## 5. Changes every vault gets

- **Large downloads read in parallel.** A presigned download (large files, large packs) reads in 8 MB ranges, 8 at a time. The CLI team measured 1.3 MB/s for one stream from a cloud sandbox and 11.8 MB/s for eight. Every range's length is checked, with one retry and then an error. A host that ignores `Range` is read in one stream as before.
- **A first push sends its refs last and on their own,** after the objects, keys and index. A first push that stops part-way is a first push again when it is retried, and never leaves refs naming objects that are not there.

## 6. Security

What the host learns from a pack vault:
- **From pack names and zip directories:** when each push happened, which commit it carried, and the sizes of its objects. This is the cost of the listing being the index (threat model row TM-R38).
- **With compression on:** how compressible each file is (TM-R40). `sgit pack import --no-deflate` makes a pack vault without compression. `init --packs` always compresses.

A pack cannot write anything a loose object could not:
- every member must be named `bare/data/obj-cas-imm-<hex>`, be stored uncompressed, and declare no more bytes than the pack holds, or it is refused by its directory entry without being read;
- a pack that names a member twice is refused whole;
- every member is checked against its content address before it is written;
- a forged pack cannot move the head, because the ref still moves only by compare-and-swap.

The feature was reviewed before release in four rounds by cli.sgit.ai's build agent, with tests, a code review and live trials. The rounds found four ways compaction could leave a fresh clone without part of the history (two in the first build, two in the fixes for them), a failed first push that could drop the root commit, a zip-bomb path, a gate that admitted older clients, and smaller issues. Each was fixed with a test. How that went is in [Four rounds to no blockers](../articles/pack-mode-four-rounds.md); the reports and the CLI team's answers are under [research](../research/topics/write-path.md).

## 7. Moving an existing vault

You do not convert a vault in place. You make a new pack vault from a full clone of it, and keep the old one:

```text
$ sgit clone <old vault key> old-full            # a full clone: no --path, no --depth
$ sgit pack import old-full new-packs            # prints the NEW vault key: save it
$ cd new-packs && sgit status                    # "This vault has never been pushed"
$ sgit push                                      # one snapshot
```

- **The new vault goes to the same server as the source.** To put it somewhere else, pass `--base-url` to the import, or run `sgit remote add origin <url>` in the new folder before pushing.
- **Hand out the new key.** Then retire the old vault when nobody uses it.
- **To go back,** `sgit pack export <pack clone> <new dir>` makes a normal vault again, with its own key. The round trip was tested end to end: identical files, the same commit messages, every signature verified.

## 8. Known limits

- No web view of a pack vault.
- `--path` and `--depth` take the packs whole; scoped reads of a snapshot are the next version.
- `clone-branch` and `clone-range` do not read packs yet.
- Compaction is manual (`sgit pack compact`). Nothing triggers it automatically. Run it when `commits/` holds more than about 50 packs, or more than a tenth of the snapshot's bytes.
- A clone that was behind when a compaction ran downloads the whole snapshot on its next pull.

*Sources: the CLI's CHANGELOG and its [pack-mode feature reference](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/tree/dev/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/22) (22 October 2026); the measurements are cli.sgit.ai's live trials of 21 and 22 October 2026 on dev.send.sgraph.ai, except the comms vault's, which are the CLI team's. Every claim in sections 4 and 6 was checked against the code at the merge to main (`ab97e497`) and on dev at `182cfc16`, and the release itself (`70b37483`, sgit-ai 0.24.0 from PyPI) was run through the playbook's recipes live on dev the evening it was published.*

# sgit-ai 0.25.0 release notes: large vaults, cli.sgit.ai

> Release notes for sgit-ai 0.25.0, for people and agents. On a large vault, the cost of a command now follows the change, not the vault. On a vault of 76,000 files a one-file commit went from 29 minutes to under 5 seconds and a status from 71 seconds to about 4. What changed (trees read as JSON, the flattened head cached, a linear and incremental tree builder, a scan cache keyed like git's index, no tree walk when a push's server has nothing new, history log by tree diff), the data-loss bug a review found in the first version of the scan cache and how it was closed, the two new cache files and what they hold, and what is still slow. Nothing changes on the server or in a vault's format.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-25-0.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit-ai 0.25.0: large vaults

The release notes for 0.25.0, written to be read by a person or handed to an agent. **Your daily loop does not change**, and nothing changes on the server or in how a vault is stored. What changes is how long a command takes on a big vault: it now follows the size of the change, not the size of the vault.

## 1. Update and check

```text
$ sgit update          # wraps: pip install --upgrade sgit-ai
$ sgit version
sgit-ai v0.25.0
```

If `sgit version` shows an older number, you have more than one Python environment. Run `python -m pip install --upgrade sgit-ai` in the one your harness uses. Existing clones need nothing.

The first `status` in each clone after the update reads and hashes every file once, to build its new scan cache. On a vault of 76,000 files that took 47 seconds. Every command after it is fast.

## 2. What it measured

The newsroom reported on 26 October that its source-watch vault had become very slow in 0.24.0. That vault holds 79,465 files in 38,474 folders and 2.7 GB:

- **`status`:** 155 s.
- **`commit`:** more than 4 minutes, whatever the commit held.
- **`push`:** about 4 minutes 15 seconds.
- **`history log`:** more than 8 minutes.

The same commands, on vaults of the same shape:

| Command | 0.24.0 | 0.25.0 | Vault |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status`, nothing changed | 70.7 s | **3.9 to 4.4 s** | 76,000 files, 58,061 folders (cli.sgit.ai) |
| `status`, one file changed | 70.8 s | **4.1 s**, the same file reported | the same |
| `commit` of one file | **1,739 s** (29 min) | **4.6 s** | the same |
| the first commit of all 76,000 files | not run | **55 s** | the same |
| `status`, nothing changed | 130 s | **7.4 s** | 228,000 files, 77,227 folders (CLI team) |
| the first commit of the whole vault | 2,846 s (47 min) | **155 s** | the same |
| `push` of one small commit | about 4 min 15 s (the newsroom's vault) | **10 to 18 s** | the same |
| `history log`, 10 commits with counts | 464 s | **7.4 s** | the same |

The cli.sgit.ai figures are local commands on a 4-core cloud sandbox, 0.24.0 from PyPI against the release code on the same clone. The CLI team's are from an in-memory host, so network time is excluded; the newsroom's include it.

## 3. What changed

- **Trees are read as the JSON they are.** 0.24.0 built a typed object for every tree, about 3 ms each: two minutes on 38,000 folders. Ids are still checked against the object-id form.
- **The flattened head is cached,** per process and on disk under `.sg_vault/local/flat-cache/<tree id>.json`. A tree id is a content address, so the cache never needs invalidating. The newest two heads are kept. The cache is versioned, validated when read, and checked against the root tree; anything wrong in it is rebuilt.
- **The tree builder is linear.** It used to scan every folder for each folder's children, which was quadratic: the 47-minute first commit.
- **A commit builds only what changed.** A file whose size and content hash match the head keeps its entry without being read. A folder whose contents are all unchanged keeps its tree id. A one-file commit builds the folders on that file's path and nothing else. The ids are exactly those a full build gives: the tests compare both, and a fuzzer of about 430 commits compared every head against a full rebuild.
- **`status` no longer hashes every file.** A scan cache (`.sg_vault/local/scan-cache.json`) records each file's hash under git's index key: modification time, change time, size, inode and device. A file is trusted only if all five match and it was last modified more than two seconds before the scan began.
- **Path checks are memoised,** and ignore rules are cached per folder. The scan takes one `lstat` per file.
- **A push no longer walks every tree when the server has nothing new.** If the server's head is the one this clone last accepted, and every object of it is local, the implicit pull skips the walk. Any doubt takes the full fetch, as before.
- **`history log` diffs each commit against its parent,** walking only where tree ids differ, instead of flattening every commit in full. Its output is byte-identical to 0.24.0's.
- **`sgit pull` lists every commit the branch gained,** with its date, even when `status` or a pack had already brought the objects. It used to print "0 new commits" in that case. The list is exact under a merge with one machine's clock behind.

## 4. A bug found before release, and closed

A review of the branch on 26 October found that the first form of the scan cache trusted a file whose size and modification time were unchanged. That form was briefly on dev as **0.24.1**, never on PyPI.

- **What went wrong:** an edit that kept a file's size and modification time was invisible. A restored mtime, `cp -p`, `rsync -t`, an unpacked zip or tar and a same-size `mv` all do that. `commit` skipped the edit, and `pull` then overwrote it with the incoming version.
- **The fix:** the cache now keys on the change time, inode and device as well, which no ordinary tool can set back. It records a file only when nothing moved while it was read. And `pull` always re-reads the files a merge would touch before it decides the working tree is clean.
- **Confirmed** with the review's three reproductions, each now behaving exactly as 0.24.0 does, and a test for each.

If you installed 0.24.1 from dev, update: its cache file is discarded and rebuilt automatically.

## 5. What is on disk now

Two new files in each clone's `.sg_vault/local/`, both readable by you alone (mode 0600):

| File | Holds | Delete it? |
|---|---|---|
| `flat-cache/<tree id>.json` | the head's paths, sizes, content hashes, types and folder tree ids; the newest two heads | safe; rebuilt on the next command |
| `scan-cache.json` | every working-copy path with its timestamps, size, inode and hash | safe; the next `status` re-reads every file |

They hold **file names in clear**, next to the vault key that is already there (threat model TM-R41):
- `history diff` against an old commit caches that commit's names, including files deleted since;
- a sparse clone caches names it never fetched.

Backups made with `sgit vault backup` do not include them. Under the proposed [sealed vault keys](../dev/sealed-vault-keys/index.md), they would be encrypted or kept in memory.

**Compatibility:**
- a clone used with 0.25.0 still works with 0.24.0, which ignores the new files;
- 0.24.0 and 0.25.0 read each other's commits as clean;
- vaults, the server and pack mode are unchanged.

## 6. Still slow, or not covered

- **A `pull` that brings commits pushed by another clone** still walks the new head's trees the old way: a minute or two on the newsroom's vault, against hours before.
- **A three-way merge,** when two clones changed the same branch, still builds the whole tree.
- **`push` still walks the working tree once** looking for `.conflict` files: about 4 s on a large vault.
- **`pull`'s list of new commits reads the clone's whole history,** about 0.4 ms a commit. That is half a second on 1,229 commits and about 2 s on 5,000, even when nothing is new.
- **On Windows,** Python's change time is the creation time. An edit that keeps a file's size and restores its modification time may still go unseen there. Linux and macOS are covered.

*Sources: the CLI's CHANGELOG and its response notes of 26 October 2026 under `team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/26/`; the newsroom's slowness report of the same day; cli.sgit.ai's two reviews of the branch, run against SGit-AI__CLI at `c6c48187` and `3ffcb5c7`, with the full test suite (4,588 passed), the review's reproductions (re-run against the PyPI package, whose code is that of `main` at `7a3b90aa`: `3ffcb5c7` with the version raised), a fuzzer of about 430 commits, and the timings above on a vault of 76,000 files.*

# sgit-ai 0.26.0 release notes: pack indexes, selective working copies, the pack store, cli.sgit.ai

> Release notes for sgit-ai 0.26.0, for people and agents. Every push to a pack vault now writes an index pack beside its data pack, so readers stop walking trees. A pull plans its fetch from the indexes, and history log reads change lists. A clone can skip writing the working copy, and an agent then checks out only the files it needs. A clone can keep the packs in place instead of unpacking hundreds of thousands of objects. A clone of one folder takes that folder by byte ranges. On a 76,000-file vault, a full clone fell from about two minutes to one, a no-checkout clone takes about 28 seconds, a one-folder clone under 3 seconds against 36, and history log half a second against three. The new agent loop, the commands, the compatibility rules (a pack vault created by 0.26.0 needs 0.26.0), what is on disk, and what is still slow. Nothing changes on the server.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-26-0.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit-ai 0.26.0: pack indexes

The release notes for 0.26.0, written to be read by a person or handed to an agent.
- **Your daily loop does not change.** `clone`, `pull`, `status`, `commit` and `push` work as before.
- **Nothing changes on the server.**
- **On pack vaults, much of the work a reader used to redo is now done once by the writer and shipped beside the pack.** The new options below let an agent take only what it needs.

The design is the dev pack [Pack indexes for sgit](../dev/pack-indexes/index.md). The story and the numbers are in [Pack indexes, shipped](../articles/pack-indexes-shipped.md).

## 1. Update and check

```text
$ sgit update          # wraps: pip install --upgrade sgit-ai
$ sgit version
sgit-ai v0.26.0
```

If `sgit version` prints a note that another `sgit` comes first on your PATH, you have two installs. Upgrade that one too, or put this one first. Existing clones need nothing.

## 2. What is new

### Index packs: on by default, nothing to do

- **What a push writes.** Every push to a pack vault uploads, beside each data pack, an **index pack** under `bare/packs/indexes/`, encrypted with the read key and signed with your clone key. It holds:
  - the commit's change list;
  - the folders it changed;
  - its generation number.
- **What a snapshot index holds.** Each compaction writes one with the head's whole file map, one entry per folder, the commit graph and two cross-references (blob to paths, file to commits).
- **What readers do with them.** They use the indexes instead of walking trees:
  - a pull plans its fetch from them;
  - a fresh clone takes its file map from them;
  - `history log` reads its counts from the change lists, fetching the indexes of archived commits when it needs them.
- **Every answer is checked.** An index is checked against the commit, its signature and its trees before use, and every object it names is still verified by its id. A missing or bad index is skipped and the reader walks as before.

**For older pack vaults:** run this once, with the write key, to give them indexes:

```text
$ sgit pack index build     # writes the index packs the vault lacks, adds the 'pack-indexes' feature
$ sgit pack index verify    # checks every index against its trees (read-only)
$ sgit pack index stats
```

### A selective working copy: the loop for agents that do not need every file

```text
$ sgit clone --no-checkout <vault key> work      # the vault's objects and index, no files written
$ cd work
$ sgit checkout sources/uk                       # write a folder (or files) you need
$ ... read, write, add files ...
$ sgit commit -m "..." && sgit push
$ sgit pull --no-checkout                        # move the head; list what changed; write nothing
$ sgit checkout --since-pull                     # write what that pull added or changed
```

- **What `status` and `commit` count.** A file never checked out is **not** a deletion. A checked-out file you delete is one. The record is `.sg_vault/local/checkout.json`; if it is lost, sgit rebuilds it from the files on disk.
- **`sgit checkout` keeps your uncommitted edits.** A path you have changed is left alone and reported as `≠ path (kept: yours, uncommitted)` unless you pass `--force`.
- **Other ways to choose files:**
  - `sgit checkout --changed-since <commit>` writes what changed since that commit;
  - `sgit checkout --all` writes everything and makes the clone a full one, but only when every file could be written.
- **A plain `sgit pull`** on a selective clone writes only the changed files you have checked out. It lists the rest, for `sgit checkout --since-pull`.

### The pack store: `clone --pack-store`

```text
$ sgit clone --pack-store <vault key> work
```

- **What it does.** A pack clone keeps the packs it downloads under `.sg_vault/bare/packs/` and reads each object from its pack by offset. It no longer unpacks hundreds of thousands of objects into `bare/data/`.
- **Every read is verified.** Each object is checked against its id when it arrives and again every time it is read.
- **Managing it:**
  - `sgit pack store status` shows the kept packs;
  - `sgit pack store extract` turns the clone into an ordinary one;
  - `sgit pack store rebuild` recovers the offset table from the packs.
- **Do not open a `--pack-store` clone with 0.25.0.** It does not know the store. Run `sgit pack store extract` first if an older client must use the folder.

### One folder of a pack vault by byte ranges: `clone --path`

```text
$ sgit clone --path sources/uk <vault key> work
```

- **What travels.** A scoped clone of a pack vault reads only what the folder needs, by ranged reads from the packs on the host. 0.25.0 downloaded every pack whole.
- **Pack order.** Packs are now written in path order, so one folder's files sit together.
- **Hosts without ranged reads.** Where the host has no presigned route (`sgit serve`, a self-hosted server), the packs come whole, as before, and the clone says so.

### Also in this release

- **The newsroom's first-morning fixes:**
  - every file sgit writes (clone, pull, checkout, branch switch) is recorded in the scan cache, so the first `status` after a clone stats files instead of reading them back;
  - a pull of another clone's pass only walks what changed: 566 s → 31.7 s measured by the CLI team on 228,000 files;
  - `sgit version` names a shadowing install.
- **From the 0.25.0 review:**
  - `pull`'s list of new commits expands its base only within a day of clock skew;
  - Windows uses its change time in the scan cache key.

## 3. What it measured

The CLI team's release measurement: a synthetic vault of 76,000 files in 58,553 folders, built by each build under test, on an in-memory host, 4 cores. Network time is excluded.

| Flow | 0.25.0 | **0.26.0** |
|---|---|---|
| full clone | 117 s | **61 s** |
| `clone --no-checkout` | n/a | **28 s** |
| `clone --pack-store` | n/a | **26 s** |
| `clone --path` of one folder (1,520 files) | 36 s, the whole 88 MB pack | **2.8 s**, 12.5 MB by ranges |
| pull of a pass, full clone | 81 s | **6.6 s** |
| push of a 5-file commit | 6.2 s | **4.5 to 5.2 s** |
| push of a 300-file pass | 12.5 s | **11.6 to 11.8 s** |
| `history log`, 4 commits | 3.2 s | **0.45 s** |
| `history log` on a fresh clone after compaction | 6.1 s | **1.1 s** |
| first push of a new vault (snapshot) | 47 s | 82 to 84 s |
| compaction | 58 s | 95 to 109 s |

cli.sgit.ai measured the released code (`09172b0f`) independently on its own 76,000-file vault: full clone 49.8 s, `--no-checkout` 33.6 s, `--pack-store` 27.7 s, `clone --path` 3.1 s, a 5-file push 5.2 s, `pull --no-checkout` 1.1 s, `history log` 0.19 s, and 0.84 s on a fresh clone after compaction; [the table](../articles/pack-indexes-shipped.md#measured). Both sets agree: everything an agent does daily is as fast or faster. The first push of a vault and each compaction now also write the snapshot index, which is the price of the rest.

## 4. Compatibility

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| **an existing pack vault, agents on 0.25.0 and 0.26.0 together** | works. 0.25.0 never reads `bare/packs/indexes/`; 0.26.0 fills the gaps 0.25.0's pushes leave. The vault's `min_client` does not change |
| **a pack vault created with 0.26.0** | **needs 0.26.0.** As since 0.24.0, a new pack vault is gated at the release that created it. Update every agent that will use it before you create it. [R3-2](../research/pack-indexes-review-round-3.md#r3-2). **Fixed for the next release:** on the CLI's `dev` (pre-release 0.26.1.dev0, `pip install --pre sgit-ai`), a new pack vault's gate is what its features need, 0.24.0; `sgit vault format --min-client` lowers an existing one |
| **a `--pack-store` clone** | only 0.26.0 opens it; `sgit pack store extract` makes it an ordinary clone |
| **`sgit pack index verify` after a compaction of an older vault** | may report wrong offsets (`at`) in the index of an archived 0.24.0 or 0.25.0 pack; no data is affected and no reader in 0.26.0 uses those offsets. [R3-1](../research/pack-indexes-review-round-3.md#r3-1) |
| **normal (loose) vaults** | unchanged |

## 5. What is on disk now

Everything below lives under `.sg_vault/local/` in each clone, readable by you alone, as in 0.25.0:

| File | Holds | Delete it? |
|---|---|---|
| `index/packs/<folder>/<name>.zip` | the index packs this clone downloaded, **still encrypted** | safe; fetched again when needed |
| `index/cd/<folder>/<name>.json` | the central directories a scoped clone read (object ids and offsets) | safe |
| `checkout.json`, `last-pull.json`, `stale.json` | a selective clone's record: the paths checked out, what the last pull changed, bytes a pull left behind | safe; rebuilt from the files on disk |
| `pack-store.sqlite` | a `--pack-store` clone's table of where each object sits in which pack | safe; `sgit pack store rebuild` |
| `generations.json`, `gaps.json` | commit generations this clone computed; data packs it pushed without an index | safe |

The flat cache and scan cache of 0.25.0 are unchanged (threat model TM-R41). The index packs add nothing in clear: they stay encrypted on disk and are opened in memory.

## 6. Still slow, or not covered

- **The first push and each compaction** take 35 to 50 s longer on a 76,000-file vault, to build the snapshot index. It is 31.6 MB beside an 88 MB pack on that vault of small files, and a few per cent on vaults with real content. Making the cross-references optional is an open decision.
- **A full clone still writes every working file.** Use `--no-checkout` and `sgit checkout` for the folders you need.
- **`status` still stats every file** it tracks: about 4 s at 76,000 files.
- **Reading one file with no clone at all** (Phase 4) is not in this release.

*Sources: the CLI's CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` section and the CLI team's documents of 26 and 27 October, published here as research: [the dev-pack review](../research/pack-indexes-dev-pack-review.md), [steps 1 to 5 shipped](../research/pack-indexes-steps-shipped.md), [their own review](../research/pack-indexes-cli-self-review.md), [the fixes](../research/pack-indexes-review-fixes.md) and [release readiness](../research/pack-indexes-release-readiness.md); cli.sgit.ai's reviews, rounds [1](../research/pack-indexes-review-round-1.md), [2](../research/pack-indexes-review-round-2.md) and [3](../research/pack-indexes-review-round-3.md), run against SGit-AI__CLI at `a9f24d86`, `58f52a42` and the dev merge `09172b0f`.*
