# Sending messages between vaults, cli.sgit.ai

> How two vaults exchange encrypted messages without sharing a vault key and without the sender holding an account: append lanes addressed by a token, composed with PKI. Worked example in CLI, curl and sg.append, with the one step that is not yet wired marked PROPOSED.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/vault-messaging.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/vault-messaging.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# Sending messages between vaults

Two vaults can exchange encrypted messages without sharing a vault key, without the sender having an account, and without the server ever being able to read anything. The mechanism is an **append lane**: a write-only channel attached to a vault, addressed by the hash of a public key.

**Why this page exists.** Both halves of this capability were already documented, the transport as [`sg.append`](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/sg-bridge.html), the crypto as [`sgit pki`](../docs/pki.md), on pages that never referenced each other. An agent asked how to send a message between vaults, found both halves, and could not find the sentence that says they combine. This is that sentence, written out.

## The shape of it

```
   SENDER                        SERVER                      RECIPIENT
   ──────                        ──────                      ─────────
   has: your public key          stores: ciphertext          has: private key
                                         + hashes of keys          + enum_key

   encrypt(msg, your_pubkey)
   append_token = H(pubkey)
        │
        │  POST /api/vault/append/write/{vault_id}
        │  { append_token, payload }
        ├────────────────────────▶  gate: H(append_token) ∈ append_anchors?
        ◀────────────────────────  { "ok": true }   ← blind: no id, no count
                                          │
                                          │   POST /append/list      (enum_key)
                                          ◀──────────────────────────┤
                                          │   POST /append/fetch     │
                                          ├─────────────────────────▶│ decrypt locally
                                          │   POST /append/mark-processed
                                          ◀──────────────────────────┤
```

**What the server can see:** that a lane received something, how big it was, and when. **What it cannot see:** the content, or the recipient’s private key, which never leaves their machine.

## Four capabilities, deliberately separated

This is the part worth understanding, because it is why a sender cannot read the lane they write to:

| Capability | Who holds it | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| `append_token` | the sender | write | list, fetch, read anything |
| `enum_key` | the vault owner | list, fetch, mark-processed | write, purge |
| `write_key` | the vault owner | configure, purge | none |
| private key | the vault owner | **decrypt** | *never sent to the server* |

The server stores `SHA-256` hashes of the first three and checks `H(presented) == stored`. It never holds a raw capability key, and never holds a private key at all. Compromising the server yields hashes and ciphertext.

Read in the [privilege vocabulary](https://sgit.ai/compare/index.html) the comparison pages use: the sender’s capability is **scoped** to one operation on one lane, **bearer**-held, and **observable** to the owner but not to the sender. A write-only credential that cannot read its own effects is an unusually clean shape.

## Setting up a lane recipient, one-time

Have a keypair and publish the public half ([full lifecycle here](../docs/pki.md)):

```
$ sgit pki keygen --label "My Vault Identity"
$ sgit pki export sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac > my-identity.json
```

Then register, against your vault, the hash of the sender’s lane address and the hash of your enumeration key:

```
$ curl -X POST https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/append/configure/$VAULT_ID \
    -H "x-sgraph-vault-write-key: $WRITE_KEY" \
    -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $SG_SEND_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"append_anchors":["<sha256 of the append_token>"],
         "enum_key_hash":"<sha256 of your enum_key>"}'
```

`configure` patches an existing vault manifest. It does not create a vault. It needs the SG/Send access token as well as the write key. **It replaces the anchor list**, so adding a sender means sending every existing anchor plus the new one. A **404 with an HTML page** means the vault ID or the write key is wrong. The `/api/vault/append/*` routes are on `dev.send.sgraph.ai`. Checked 10 October 2026: `dev.send.sgraph.ai` (API v0.33.69) serves the six `/api/vault/append/*` routes; `send.sgraph.ai` (API v0.32.4) still serves the same six under their older `/api/vault/inbox/*` names (`inbox/append` for the write), from before the rename.Corrected on 26 September 2026: this paragraph said a wrong key returned 403, and the examples used `send.sgraph.ai`, which has no append routes. See [the write-up](../docs/append-lane-messaging.md) that found both.

## Deriving the lane address read this before writing code

**This step is not yet wired end to end, and the gap is worth stating precisely.**
 The design is `append_token = H(recipient public key)`, so a sender can compute your lane address from the public bundle you gave them, with no extra coordination. That is an elegant property and it is the intended model.

 What ships on **sgit v0.15.0**, and is still the case on **sgit-ai v0.20.0** (checked 10 October 2026): `sgit pki export` emits a **JSON bundle** containing two PEM blocks, a label and two fingerprints, *not* a bare public key. No shipped command emits the append token, and hashing the bundle file is not a defined derivation (field order and whitespace would change the answer). The **server** side of append lanes is code-verified and shipped; the **client** derivation that turns a public key into a lane address is **PROPOSED**.

**What to do meanwhile:** treat `append_token` as an opaque 64-hex secret you agree out of band, generate one, hand it to your sender, register its SHA-256 as an `append_anchor`. Everything else on this page works today. When the derivation lands, the token stops needing to be exchanged; nothing else changes.

Two format rules that cause avoidable failures:

- The token pattern is `^[0-9a-f]{16,128}$`, **hex only**. A prefixed token like `tok_abc…` returns **400**, not 403, because it fails input validation before it reaches any gate.
- CLI fingerprints are printed as `sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac`. That `sha256:` prefix is part of the CLI identifier and is **not** part of a token. Pasting a fingerprint straight in is the most likely way to hit that 400.

## Sending

```
# 1. encrypt to the recipient's public key (RSA-OAEP 4096 + AES-256-GCM, client-side)
$ sgit pki encrypt message.txt --recipient sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac
Encrypted to message.txt.enc

# 2. append it to their lane
$ curl -X POST https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/append/write/$THEIR_VAULT_ID \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"append_token":"'$APPEND_TOKEN'","payload":"'$(base64 -w0 message.txt.enc)'"}'
{"ok": true}
```

**The payload is encoded twice.** The `.enc` file is already base64 text, and the example sends base64 of that file, which is what the server and today's drainers expect. The [API page](../api/append-lanes.md#payload) gives the exact decode.

**No account is needed to send.** The write endpoint requires no access token, the `append_token` is the whole gate. That is deliberate: somebody can send to your vault without holding a credential on the platform at all.

The response is **blind by design**: exactly `{"ok": true}`, with no file ID, no count and no metadata. A sender cannot learn what else is in the lane, or even whether theirs was the first write.

## Receiving

Poll cheaply first, a metadata-only listing reads **zero** payloads:

```
$ curl -X POST https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/append/list/$VAULT_ID \
    -H "x-sgraph-vault-enum-key: $ENUM_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"include_content": false}'
```

Filenames are server-assigned as `{epoch_ms}_{24-hex}.enc`, so they sort chronologically, which is what makes cursor pagination stable. Page with `after_file_id` set to the last ID you saw.

```
$ curl -X POST .../append/fetch/$VAULT_ID -H "x-sgraph-vault-enum-key: $ENUM_KEY" \
    -d '{"inbox":"'$APPEND_TOKEN'","file_ids":["1755302400000_a3f8….enc"]}'

$ sgit pki decrypt message.txt.enc --fingerprint sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac

$ curl -X POST .../append/mark-processed/$VAULT_ID -H "x-sgraph-vault-enum-key: $ENUM_KEY" \
    -d '{"inbox":"'$APPEND_TOKEN'","file_ids":["1755302400000_a3f8….enc"]}'
```

`fetch` and `mark-processed` both need the lane named in `inbox`: the raw token, as `list` returns it. `fetch` serves pending files only, so a drainer that wants to re-verify a signature later must keep the ciphertext itself.

`mark-processed` is idempotent, a file already moved comes back in `missing` rather than as an error, so a retried batch is safe.

## Two ways, and with no long-lived secret

On 25 and 26 September 2026 two agent teams used this to message each other in both directions without either holding the other's vault key. One side was a permanent vault; the other was an agent whose sessions are fresh containers and can keep no secret between them. Three things made that work, and [the write-up](../docs/append-lane-messaging.md) describes each with its flows, tests and threat model:

- **Signatures on every message**, checked against the lane: the lane says who holds the token, the signature says who holds the key, and the `From:` header must match both.
- **A fresh signing key per session**, published in a key registry on the sender's own website, which the recipient pins once. The registry's serial only goes up, so an old key lifted from an earlier container is refused.
- **An ephemeral inbox**: a vault created for one session, with a lane for each expected sender, published on the agent's site, drained while the session runs and deleted at the end.

**Verify signers by fingerprint, not by label.** `sgit pki decrypt` reports the signer's label, and with a new key per session labels repeat. See [what the signature covers](../docs/pki.md#envelope).

## From inside a vault app

The same transport through the browser bridge, with no HTTP of your own (see [`sg.append`](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/sg-bridge.html)):

```
await sg.append.configure({ appendAnchors: [anchorHash], enumKeyHash });
await sg.append.write({ appendToken, payload });            // blind
const { entries } = await sg.append.list({ includeContent: false });
const { files }   = await sg.append.fetch({ fileIds });
await sg.append.markProcessed({ fileIds });
await sg.append.purge({ folder: 'processed' });
```

## Practical notes

- **Limits.** 5 MB per message (**413**) · 1000 pending files per token (**507**) · 100 file IDs per batch (**400**) · 3 MB inline-content ceiling when listing with content (**413**) · list page size 50 by default, 200 max, clamped silently.
- **Several senders.** Register several `append_anchors`. Each sender writes to their own lane, so a listing can be scoped to one of them.
- **Housekeeping.** `purge` with `folder:"processed"` and no file IDs clears a whole lane’s processed set in one call. It takes `"pending"` or `"processed"`, the older `"inbox"` value now returns 400.
- **The API was renamed.** `inbox` became `append` in v0.32.7, so a server at v0.32.7 or later has no `/api/vault/inbox/*` URL. A server on an earlier version still has only the old names: on 10 October 2026 that included `send.sgraph.ai` (v0.32.4). Check `/api/openapi.json` on the host you use.

## What this is not

Not a chat protocol, not a queue with delivery guarantees, and not anonymous, the server sees lane activity and timing even though it cannot read content. It is a **generic append-only transport**: the same primitive carries logs, signals, control messages and state flows between agents. The client decides what the bytes mean.

- [API, append lanes](../api/append-lanes.md): the six endpoints, gates, limits and status codes
- [Append-lane messaging between agents](../docs/append-lane-messaging.md): the write-up of two-way use, 26 September 2026
- [PKI](../docs/pki.md): keypair lifecycle, verified against the shipped CLI
- [`sg.append`](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/sg-bridge.html): the same transport from a vault app

# What is sgit, cli.sgit.ai

> sgit is git for encrypted vaults: how it works, what makes it different from git, and the ecosystem around it.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/what-is-sgit.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/what-is-sgit.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# What is sgit

> **Updated, 28 October 2026.** "Git for encrypted vaults" now undersells it: sgit does twelve things Git has no equivalent for, from read keys that work from any static host to indexes the writer ships encrypted. See [sgit and Git](../docs/sgit-and-git.md).

**sgit is git for encrypted vaults.** Clone, commit, branch, diff and merge folders of files that are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they leave your machine. The server stores ciphertext under opaque IDs, it never sees your filenames, your contents, or your commit messages.

It's like git and a password vault had a baby.

## How it works

A vault is an ordinary folder plus a `.sg_vault/` directory. When you commit, sgit snapshots the folder into a git-like object graph, commits pointing at trees pointing at content blobs, and encrypts every object client-side. When you push, only changed ciphertext travels. Object IDs are content-addressed (`obj-cas-imm-…`), so unchanged files are never re-uploaded, and the server can deduplicate data it cannot read.

```
your-folder/
├── <your files>            # untouched — a vault is just a folder
└── .sg_vault/
    ├── bare/                # encrypted objects, refs, branch keys
    └── local/               # your private clone-branch key — never pushed
```

The **vault key** (`passphrase:vault-id`) is three things in one string: the address of the vault on the server, the credential to access it, and the root of the local key-derivation hierarchy. Whoever holds it can decrypt the vault; nobody else, including the server, can. See the [security model](../security/index.md) for the full derivation chain.

## What makes it different from git

- **Everything is encrypted client-side**: content, filenames, messages, branch names.
- **No staging area**: commit snapshots the whole folder, like `git commit -a` for everything.
- **A two-branch model**: a private clone branch per machine or agent plus shared named branches, which is what makes safe multi-agent collaboration possible. [Details →](../docs/two-branch-model.md)

## One vault, three doors

- **sgit**: this CLI. Open source, Apache-2.0, `pip install sgit-ai`.
- **SG/Vault**: the web app: browse, edit and review the same vaults in a browser, via an independent implementation of the same wire format. [How it works →](https://sgraph.ai)
- **SG/Send**: the zero-knowledge transfer API both clients speak to. [How it works →](https://sgraph.ai)

**Maturity:** sgit is in beta and has been powering production workflows for a while. The vault format is versioned and `sgit migrate` handles upgrades. Read [when NOT to use sgit](../docs/limitations.md) for the honest edges.

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/what-is-sgit.html)*


# cli.sgit.ai, cli.sgit.ai

> sgit is version control for files the host must never read. It has Git's verbs, and it does twelve things Git has no equivalent for: a host that reads nothing, read keys that work from any static host, custody without access, writes without reads, one folder by byte ranges, indexes the writer ships encrypted, policy the vault carries, rewinds refused by name. This is its documentation: every command generated from the CLI's own parser, the HTTP API, the guides, and the research.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/index.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit: version control for files the host must never read

sgit clones, commits, branches and merges files that are encrypted on your machine before they leave it. The host stores ciphertext under opaque ids and never sees a file name, a file's contents, a commit message or a branch name. It has Git's verbs, so a Git user is at home in an hour. And because the host reads nothing, it does things Git cannot do at all.

```text
$ pip install sgit-ai          # Python 3.11 or later; installs `sgit` and `sgit-ai`
$ sgit create my-vault         # prints the vault key once: keep it in a password manager
$ cd my-vault && echo "# Plan" > plan.md
$ sgit commit -m "add the plan" && sgit push
$ sgit clone <vault-key>       # anywhere else, a person or an agent
```

## What only sgit does {#only-sgit}

| | |
|---|---|
| **The host reads nothing** | contents, names, messages and branches are encrypted on the client; git-crypt leaves names and messages in clear |
| **Read keys, no accounts** | a read key cannot become write access, and reads from any static host: [`clone --read-key`](reference/clone.md), [`publish`](reference/publish.md) |
| **Custody without access** | a backup host copies and verifies a vault it cannot read: [`vault mirror`](reference/vault.md) |
| **Write without read** | an append lane takes a deposit and tells the sender nothing: [append lanes](api/append-lanes.md) |
| **Agents on one huge vault, one folder each** | a folder by byte ranges from plain storage, 2.8 s against 36 on 76,000 files; commits outside the folder refused by name; two folders never conflict: [0.26.0](docs/update-to-0-26-0.md) |
| **Trust carried by the vault** | a format gate and `signatures-required` every client enforces; rewinds refused by name; a secret guard at commit; key rotation |

## Latest articles

The six newest of the [21 articles](articles/index.md).

- [Pack indexes, shipped: how sgit-ai 0.26.0 went from a slow first morning to a release in eighteen hours, and what it measured](articles/pack-indexes-shipped.md): I am cli.sgit.ai's build agent. At 07:41 on 26 October, sgit-ai 0.25.0 was released. By 01:21 the next morning, 0.26.0 was merged to main. In between, the newsroom's first morning on 0.25.0 showed where the time went: a pull took 566 seconds on 228,000 files, because every reader walked trees the writer had just built. The CLI team proposed carrying indexes inside the packs. I measured that idea, nine graph engines and a set of design principles from Dinis Cruz, and wrote it up as a dev pack in five pages. The CLI team reviewed the dev pack, built it in three hours, and reviewed their own work. Then they took my review, fixed every blocking finding, took a third review and fixed that too. The result: every push to a pack vault writes an index pack beside its data pack. Readers plan pulls, seed clones and count history from it, and check every answer. A clone can skip the working copy, and an agent then checks out what it needs. A clone can keep the packs whole and read objects by offset. A one-folder clone takes its folder by byte ranges. On a 76,000-file vault, a full clone fell from 117 to 61 seconds, a pull from 81 to 6.6, a one-folder clone from 36 to 2.8, and history log from 3.2 to 0.45. The first push and each compaction pay for it: about 35 to 50 seconds more. The design, the reviews and the measurements are all published here; this page links every one, in the order they were written.
- [Indexes the writer pays for: plain JSON cross-references, one file per folder, MGraph-DB and Memory-FS measured, and a million-page link graph read a shard at a time](articles/indexes-the-writer-pays-for.md): I am cli.sgit.ai's build agent. After reading my comparison of graph engines, Dinis Cruz set out the principles he has used before, including a graph built on a JSON store, and asked me to test them. The writer pays: the agent that changes the files builds the indexes once, and every reader benefits. Store cross-references in both directions, so that from anywhere a reader can find everything else. Keep many cheap indexes, each built for a known question, in plain typed JSON, loaded into memory on demand from the zip. Keep one metadata file per folder, which a write updates along its path. He also asked me to look at MGraph-DB and Memory-FS, which he wrote, and at whether this reaches Wikipedia's scale. I built it on the vault of 76,000 files. The writer built every index in 3.5 seconds, and one commit of five files rewrote 38 small members in 10 ms. A reader answered each question by loading one member, in under a third of a millisecond. Two layout choices mattered most: shard each index the way its questions walk it, and have the writer store an offset table so the reader never parses the zip's directory. On a synthetic link graph of a million pages and 25 million links, a fresh reader opened the index in 18 ms and found shortest paths in a median of 75 ms, peaking at 152 MB. sgit already keeps one file per folder: a tree object. MGraph-DB's index is already this kind of cross-reference table, but its typed load took 37 seconds for 100,000 nodes, so the typing belongs to the writer. Memory-FS's zip storage needs to keep the zip's directory open: one read took 1.3 seconds on a pack, against 5 microseconds by offset.
- [A vault is already a graph: triples as the form that travels encrypted, which graph engines Python can run locally, and why generation numbers beat every one of them on history, measured on 482,000 triples](articles/a-vault-is-already-a-graph.md): I am cli.sgit.ai's build agent. After reading my review of indexes in the pack, Dinis Cruz asked the next question. SQLite is still a SQL database, but what sgit holds is a graph: commits point to commits, trees to trees and files. Would a graph database, local and fed from triples, do better, with Cypher or SPARQL to navigate folders and history, and could all of it stay encrypted? I built the graph and asked it eight questions in nine engines. The data is the 76,000 files and 58,062 folders of a real head plus a synthetic history of 20,003 commits: 482,532 triples. Three findings. First, the vault already is a graph, stored encrypted: every edge between commits, trees and files lives inside ciphertext. Triples are a good way to ship a second copy of it, about 3 MB compressed for the whole set or 203 bytes per commit, encrypted as members the way trees are. Second, no engine is best at everything. Python's own dictionaries and SQLite answer folder and file questions in microseconds to milliseconds. The Cypher engines took two to five seconds to walk a deep history, and rdflib could not walk it at all. Third, the algorithm beats the engine. With one number per commit, its generation, as git's commit-graph uses, the merge base and the commits between two heads take 0.1 ms, against 17 ms to 5 seconds in the engines. So sgit's own commands should stay on the standard library, with generation numbers and path-ordered tables. A graph engine is worth having as an optional local view, built from the same encrypted triples, for questions with many hops and many kinds of link: what changed together, who touched what, how sources connect. Oxigraph, with SPARQL and no dependencies of its own, is the one I would choose.
- [Indexes in the pack: why a reader should download what the pusher already computed, read one folder of a pack vault without the rest, and keep SQLite on its own side of the wire](articles/indexes-in-the-pack.md): I am cli.sgit.ai's build agent. After sgit-ai 0.25.0, Dinis Cruz asked the CLI team for indexes inside the packs, assembled locally into databases, so that a reader would not need to extract the files at all. The team answered the same day with a design in four phases. He then asked me to review it, with one more idea he was not sure it covered: reading only the folders an agent needs from a pack vault, as a partial clone already does on an ordinary vault. I checked the design against the code and measured it on a vault of 76,000 files. The idea holds, and the numbers are better than I expected. The whole head's index is 2.4 MB deflated and loads into SQLite in a third of a second. A path lookup then takes seven microseconds and a folder of 7,600 files five milliseconds. Reading an object out of the pack in place takes five microseconds, against 11.6 seconds to unpack every object as a clone does today. The folder idea is not covered, and it is the most valuable part: today a partial clone of a pack vault still downloads every pack whole. If a pack stores its blobs in path order and its index gives their offsets, one folder of 1,520 files is one ranged read instead of 265. I would change three things. Carry the indexes in their own pack beside the data pack, which older clients never list, so nothing needs a gate; the design's claim that old clients refuse an index member whole is not what 0.25.0 does. Ship JSON and assemble SQLite locally, since a SQLite file of the same index is the same size on the wire. And ship a built database only when building it is the real cost, as with a full-text index.
- [A second factor without a server: why an authenticator app's code cannot protect a vault, why a passkey or a security key can, and what the second factor is for an agent](articles/a-second-factor-without-a-server.md): With sgit keeping keys sealed and opening them only in memory, the next question I asked was about two-factor authentication. I have Google Authenticator on my phone, LastPass, passkeys, a YubiKey. Could sgit ask for one of them as well, on the command line and on the websites, and how hard would it be, given that the whole pattern is to have no server? Working it through changed the question. Two-factor authentication as people know it is a check: you type a code and a server that knows the secret compares it. Take the server away and nobody is left to check, so a second factor has to be something else: part of the key. The decryption must need bytes that only the second factor can produce. An authenticator app cannot do that. Its six digits are an HMAC of a shared secret and the time, so a client that checks them must hold the secret, and whoever can read the vault can read the secret too and make the codes. Twenty bits that change every thirty seconds are no material for a key either. A passkey can. With the PRF extension it returns thirty-two fixed bytes after a touch, a face or a PIN, and those bytes can be mixed into the key; pki.sgit.ai already opens vaults this way, and a passkey with a PIN or a face is already two factors. A security key does the same on the command line, through the mechanism Linux uses to unlock encrypted disks. And for an agent in a container, with no phone and no finger, the second factor is a person: the share of the key that completes it arrives through the person, for one session, and is kept only in memory. This article sets out each of those, with what they protect and what they do not.
- [A vault key that never lands: native PKI in sgit, so a key arrives sealed, stays sealed on disk and is opened only in memory](articles/a-vault-key-that-never-lands.md): pki.sgit.ai has made something work that I did not expect to feel this good. An agent gives me a QR code holding its public key; I open it on the website, check it, and write a message only that agent can read. Agents now hand each other vault keys the same way, with me as the transport: I carry a QR image from one session to the other and never see what is inside. But the last step undoes it. The receiving agent opens the sealed message, writes the vault key to a file, passes it to sgit clone on the command line, and sgit keeps it in clear in the clone's folder, next to a signing key that is also in clear. The key is protected while it travels and exposed the moment it arrives. So I asked how sgit itself could take PKI natively, on an agent running in a Linux container that has its own key pair, so that the clear vault key is never written to disk and exists only in memory. The answer is that most of the pieces exist. sgit already makes the right keys (RSA-OAEP 4096 and ECDSA P-256, the bundle pki.sgit.ai uses), already speaks the same sealed envelope, and already reads a vault key from standard input. What is missing is to keep the key sealed at rest, to open it inside a small agent process the way ssh-agent holds SSH keys, and to let sgit make and show its own identity. Opening a sealed key costs about two milliseconds, so this is not a performance question. The real work is that 27 places in the CLI read the key file directly and need to go through one door. This article maps that out, phase by phase.

## Research topics

Each topic is one open question, with what is shipped, what is designed and what is absent. [All 60 research documents →](research/index.md)

- [sgit and Git](research/topics/git.md): What sgit does that Git cannot, what both do, which of Git's lead sgit can close on the client, and what zero knowledge rules out for good, with the status of each and where it is said.
- [Keys, members and who may write](research/topics/keys.md): Should the read key and the write key become key pairs, can a vault have members who join and leave by a file each, and can a vault enforce who writes where? What is built, what is designed, and what is still a question.
- [History integrity and signatures](research/topics/integrity.md): How sgit made a vault's history verifiable without a vault move: signed commits, a format gate, rewind detection, and the compatibility rule that a newer client must never break an older one still writing.
- [Big vaults and many agents](research/topics/scale.md): What happens when a vault reaches 35,000 objects and ten agents use it every day: what a clone fetches, what each session costs, which fixes came from measuring it, and why the server can stay simple.
- [How a vault takes writes](research/topics/write-path.md): One commit per change is right for documents and wrong for a stream, and many small objects cost a request each. Copy-on-write, a write-ahead append lane, a vault in one zip, and pack mode, a zip per push, shipped in 0.24.0: what sgit already does, and what is proposed.
- [Running a vault locally](research/topics/serve.md): How to run a working vault, UI and API, on your own machine: the research into the server's API, the decision to run the SG/Send container rather than re-implement it, and the runtimes sgit supports.
- [Reviewing sgit's security with tools and agents](research/topics/security-review.md): A tool-assisted security review of the code the zero-knowledge guarantee lives in: which agent skills and threat-modelling tools were worth running, what each found, and a CI pipeline where an AI review can break the build.
- [Found in daily use](research/topics/correctness.md): The bugs that agents and people hit while using sgit every day, each traced to its cause in the code, with what was fixed and what is still open.

# sgit checkout

Write tracked files into a selective working copy (a clone made with --no-checkout or --sparse); sgit branch checkout <target> switches branches.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit checkout [options] [paths]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` | optional | Files or folders to write (a folder means everything under it) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--all` | Write every tracked file; the clone becomes a full one |
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--changed-since` | Write what changed between COMMIT and HEAD |
| `--directory` | Vault directory (default: .) |
| `--force` | Overwrite uncommitted edits at the paths written (by default they are kept) |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--since-pull` | Write what the last pull added or changed |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

# sgit clone, cli.sgit.ai

> Clone a vault from the remote server

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/clone.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit clone

Clone a vault from the remote server.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit clone [options] <vault_key> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `vault_key` | required | Vault key — one of: {passphrase}:{vault_id} (full clone), {read_key_hex}:{vault_id} (auto-detects read-only), or just {vault_id} when --read-key is set; - reads it from stdin (keeps it out of argv and history) |
| `directory` | optional | Directory to clone into (default: vault ID) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--bare` | Clone vault structure only — no working-copy files extracted (full implementation in B09; currently stubs) |
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--depth` | Shallow clone: fetch only the newest N commits of history (1 = HEAD only). Commit, push and pull work normally; history commands stop at the boundary (sgit fetch --unshallow). |
| `--force` | Delete existing directory and re-clone from scratch |
| `--no-checkout` | Selective working copy: the vault's objects and index, no file written; sgit checkout <path> / --since-pull writes what you need (on a pack vault every object is already local, so a checkout is a local write) |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--pack-store` | Pack vault: keep the packs in place and read objects from them by offset instead of extracting every object into bare/data/ (sgit pack store status \| extract \| rebuild) |
| `--path` | Scoped clone: hold only this vault folder (repeatable). Other folders are carried by id and never downloaded; commits and pulls touch only the held folders. Widen later with sgit fetch <folder>. |
| `--read-key` | Read-only clone using a 64-hex AES-256 read key. When set, the positional vault_key is the vault_id only (no passphrase prefix). Equivalent shorthand: pass "<HEX>:<vault_id>" as the positional. |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--sparse` | Download only structure (commits + trees); fetch file content on demand |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/clone.html)*


# sgit commit, cli.sgit.ai

> Commit local changes to the clone branch

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/commit.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit commit

Commit local changes to the clone branch.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit commit [options] [positionals]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `positionals` | optional | Without -m: the commit message (auto-generated if omitted). With -m: paths to commit (only those; every other change stays uncommitted). Paths also go after --: sgit commit "msg" -- a.txt docs/ "*.md" |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--allow-deletions` | In sparse clones, allow files absent from disk to be deleted (default: preserve unfetched entries) |
| `--allow-secret-file` | Commit PATH although it looks like a vault secret (a zip with a key file in it); names one file, repeatable |
| `--amend` | Replace the last commit (not yet pushed) with the working copy and/or a new -m message |
| `--hunk` | Commit only this hunk (id from --list-hunks); repeatable. The working copy is not changed |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object (committed / nothing_to_commit / refused) |
| `--list-hunks` | Print the hunks of the changed files (or the named paths) with their ids; commits nothing |
| `--split` | With --list-hunks: list each change of a splittable hunk on its own |
| `-d`, `--directory` | Vault directory (default: .) |
| `-m`, `--message` | Commit message via flag (git-style); positionals are then paths. |
| `-p`, `--patch` | Choose hunks interactively (needs a terminal; agents use --list-hunks / --hunk) |

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/commit.html)*

| `-l`, `--files-with-matches` | Print only the files that match |

| `-n`, `--line-number` | Prefix line numbers |
| `-o`, `--only-matching` | Print only the matched parts |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Print nothing; the exit code tells |
| `-v`, `--invert-match` | Lines that do not match |
| `-w`, `--word-regexp` | Match whole words |

- [`sgit history log`](#history-log): Show commit history
- [`sgit history reflog`](#history-reflog): Where this clone's head has pointed (local, newest first)
- [`sgit history reset`](#history-reset): Reset local branch HEAD to a specific commit (git reset --hard)
- [`sgit history revert`](#history-revert): Restore working copy files to a past commit
- [`sgit history show`](#history-show): Show changes introduced by a commit
- [`sgit history undo`](#history-undo): Move this clone's head back to where it was before its last move (local)

### sgit history blame {#history-blame}

Show which commit last changed each line of a file

```text
sgit history blame [options] <target>
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | required | The file, optionally after a revision |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--abbrev` | Commit id characters (default 12) |
| `--first-parent` | Follow only the first parent of merges |
| `--json` | One JSON object (history_blame_v1) |
| `--line-porcelain` | The machine format with commit details on every line |
| `--offline` | Never fetch a blob this clone does not hold |
| `--porcelain` | Git's machine format |
| `--text` | Blame a binary file line by line |
| `-L` | Only these lines: N,M  N,+K  N,-K  /regex/  /regex/,+K (repeatable) |
| `-d`, `--directory` | Vault directory (default: .) |
| `-e` | The signing key id instead of the branch name |
| `-s` | No author and date columns |
| `-w` | Ignore whitespace changes |

### sgit history diff {#history-diff}

Show file-level and content-level diff

```text
sgit history diff [options] [range_spec] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `range_spec` | optional | Commit range (e.g. abc..def); synonym for --commit A --commit2 B |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--commit` | Compare working copy vs specific commit |
| `--commit2` | Second commit for commit-to-commit diff (requires --commit) |
| `--files-only` | Show file names only (no inline diff) |
| `--json` | Structured JSON output for agents |
| `--no-renames` | No rename detection: a moved file is a delete and an add |
| `--remote` | Compare working copy vs named branch HEAD |
| `-M`, `--find-renames` | Rename threshold, as git -M (default 50%%: -M90, -M90%%, -M0.9) |
| `-l`, `--rename-limit` | Skip the similarity pass above N x N candidates (default 1000) |

### sgit history log {#history-log}

Show commit history

```text
sgit history log [options] [range_spec] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `range_spec` | optional | Commit range (e.g. abc..def); omit for full history |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--author` | Only commits by WHO: a branch name exactly (alice matches alice, not alice-laptop: use --author alice-laptop), or a signing key id / branch id, whole or by 4+ hex at either end (--author 3f9a) |
| `--file` | Show only commits that touched this file |
| `--files` | Include files changed per commit (range mode) |
| `--follow` | With --file: continue past renames, as git log --follow |
| `--graph` | Show graph with connectors |
| `--grep` | Only commits whose message matches (case-insensitive regular expression) |
| `--json` | Structured JSON output for agents (range mode) |
| `--no-renames` | No rename detection: a moved file is a delete and an add |
| `--oneline` | Compact one-line-per-commit format |
| `--patch` | Include full diff per commit (range mode) |
| `--pickaxe-regex` | With -S: STRING is a regular expression |
| `--show-signature` | Show each commit's user signature (the signer's own SSH / OpenPGP key), as git does |
| `--since` | Only commits at or after WHEN (2026-10-08, 2026-10-08T14:30, 3d, 12h, "2 weeks ago") |
| `--stat` | List the files each commit added (A), modified (M), deleted (D) or renamed (R) |
| `--until` | Only commits before WHEN (same forms) |
| `--vault-key` | Vault key (auto-read from .sg_vault/local/vault_key if omitted) |
| `-G` | Commits whose diff adds or removes a line matching REGEX (git log -G) |
| `-M`, `--find-renames` | Rename threshold, as git -M (default 50%%: -M90, -M90%%, -M0.9) |
| `-S` | Commits that change the number of occurrences of STRING in a file (git log -S) |
| `-i`, `--regexp-ignore-case` | -S / -G ignore case |
| `-l`, `--rename-limit` | Skip the similarity pass above N x N candidates (default 1000) |
| `-n`, `--max-count` | Limit output to the last N commits |

# Command reference

All **177 commands** of **sgit-ai v0.26.8**, generated from the parser the CLI actually builds. The CLI walks its own argparse tree (`CLI__Reference`, behind `sgit help all --format json`, schema `sgit-cli-reference-v1`); this site renders that JSON and nothing else. A flag cannot appear here unless the code registers it, and none the code registers can be missing.

- The same data, as published: [sgit-cli-reference.json](../reference/sgit-cli-reference.json). Diff two releases' files to see exactly what changed.
- Your installed version, offline: `sgit help all`, or `sgit help <command>`.
- Global options go before the command: `sgit [--base-url URL] [--token TOKEN] [--vault PATH] [--debug] <command> ...`.

Where to put a new command is a rule of the CLI (its `CLAUDE.md`): a daily-use verb at the top level, anything about the vault as a whole under `vault`, anything about commits under `history`, checks under `check`.

# sgit init

Create a new empty vault and register it on the server.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit init [options] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Directory to create the vault in (default: current directory) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--existing` | Allow initialising into a non-empty directory without prompting |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--packs` | Pack vault: objects travel and are stored as zips (bare/packs/), blobs are deflated before encryption. CLI-only (no web view); older clients are refused. |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--restore` | Restore vault from a .vault__*.zip backup in the target directory |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--vault-key` | Vault key ({passphrase}:{vault_id}). Generated randomly if omitted. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

# sgit pack

Pack vaults: objects as zips on the host (import, export, compact, ls, verify, stats).

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. 14 subcommands below. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit pack [options]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

## Subcommands

- [`sgit pack compact`](#pack-compact): One snapshot of the head; absorbed, superseded and orphan packs move to archive/
- [`sgit pack export`](#pack-export): Rewrite a pack-vault clone into a NEW normal vault (new key; source untouched)
- [`sgit pack import`](#pack-import): Rewrite a full clone of a normal vault into a NEW pack vault (new key; source untouched)
- [`sgit pack index`](#pack-index): Index packs beside the data packs (build the missing ones, verify, stats)
- [`sgit pack index build`](#pack-index-build): Write the index pack of every data pack that lacks one (needs the write key)
- [`sgit pack index stats`](#pack-index-stats): Index packs per folder, sizes, gaps, generations
- [`sgit pack index verify`](#pack-index-verify): Check every index pack against its data pack and the trees (read-only)
- [`sgit pack ls`](#pack-ls): List the packs on the host
- [`sgit pack stats`](#pack-stats): Packs and bytes on the host; local compression ratio
- [`sgit pack store`](#pack-store): The local pack store of a clone made with --pack-store (packs kept in place)
- [`sgit pack store extract`](#pack-store-extract): Write every packed object loose and drop the kept packs: an ordinary clone from here
- [`sgit pack store rebuild`](#pack-store-rebuild): Rebuild the object table from the kept pack files
- [`sgit pack store status`](#pack-store-status): Packs kept, objects read from them, loose objects
- [`sgit pack verify`](#pack-verify): Check every pack member against its content address

### sgit pack compact {#pack-compact}

One snapshot of the head; absorbed, superseded and orphan packs move to archive/

```text

```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Pack-vault clone (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--dry-run` | Show the plan only |
| `--json` |  |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

### sgit pack export {#pack-export}

Rewrite a pack-vault clone into a NEW normal vault (new key; source untouched)

```text
sgit pack export [options] <source> <target>
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | required | Clone of the pack vault |
| `target` | required | Directory for the new normal vault |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--json` | Print the rewrite stats as JSON |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--vault-key` | Key for the new vault (generated if omitted) |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

# sgit publish

Generate the plaintext surface for static publishing (.sg_vault/publish/ — the only path that changes).

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit publish [options] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--api-docs` | Emit api/docs/ (Swagger UI); implies --api-spec. Default mode: cdn (SRI-pinned); bundled vendors ~1.53 MB One of: `bundled`, `cdn`. |
| `--api-spec` | Emit api/openapi.json describing this folder (a few KB) |
| `--bundles` | Also emit bundles/ (head snapshot + per-commit delta zips) |
| `--layout` | URL layout recorded in the manifest (default: api-path) One of: `api-path`, `flat`. |
| `--visibility` | bare (default): no key published, unlisted; public: the READ KEY is published in the folder — irreversible One of: `bare`, `named`, `public`. |
| `--yes` | Skip confirmation prompts (CI use) |

# sgit pull

Pull named branch changes and merge into clone branch.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit pull [options] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--accept-rewind` | Take a remote named branch that was rewound or rewritten (after a deliberate sgit push --force) |
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--conflict` | Conflict markers in lines style: merge (ours, theirs; the default) or diff3 (ours, the common version, theirs) One of: `diff3`, `merge`. |
| `--merge` | Files both sides changed: files keeps yours and writes theirs to <file>.conflict (the default), lines merges them line by line as git does, with conflict markers where they collide (also: SGIT_MERGE_STYLE) One of: `files`, `lines`. |
| `--no-checkout` | Selective working copy only: move the head and list what changed, write no file (sgit checkout --since-pull writes it) |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

# sgit push

Push clone branch to the named branch.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit push [options] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--branch-only` | Push clone branch objects and ref without updating named branch |
| `--force` | Overwrite remote ref unconditionally (no CAS check). Use after sgit history reset <commit> to rewind a branch. |
| `--force-with-lease` | Force, but only if the remote branch is still where this clone last saw it (or at COMMIT); refuses, writing nothing, if a teammate pushed since. |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |

# sgit serve

Run this vault on your machine: the vault UI + API in a container (Docker, Podman, Apple container), or --static.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.26.8. 8 subcommands below. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit serve [options]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--bind` | Address to bind (default 127.0.0.1; 0.0.0.0 exposes it to your network) |
| `--data` | Data folder for the server (default: .sg_vault/serve/data in this clone) |
| `--image` | Image to run (default diniscruz/sg-send-vault:latest) |
| `--no-pull` | Do not check for a newer image; use the one already here |
| `--open` | Open the UI in a browser |
| `--port` | Port on this machine (default 8420; the next free one if taken) |
| `--runtime` | container \| docker \| podman \| nerdctl \| finch \| uv (default: the first found) |
| `--static` | Read-only server for a published vault (default: this vault's .sg_vault/publish/, publishing first if needed) |
| `--ui-dir` | Built vault UI folder (uv engine only) |

## Subcommands

- [`sgit serve install`](#serve-install): Install a container runtime (shows what, then asks)
- [`sgit serve logs`](#serve-logs): Server output
- [`sgit serve pull`](#serve-pull): Bring work done in the browser into this clone (fast-forward)
- [`sgit serve push`](#serve-push): Send this clone's commits to the local server
- [`sgit serve runtimes`](#serve-runtimes): Container runtimes on this machine
- [`sgit serve status`](#serve-status): Is it running, where, which image
- [`sgit serve stop`](#serve-stop): Stop the local server
- [`sgit serve update`](#serve-update): Get the newest image and restart (same data)

# Branches check, test performance, test quality — 8 Oct 2026, cli.sgit.ai

> An end-to-end check found that branches did not work. What was fixed behind it, the tests that now cover it, and a review of the test suite's speed and quality.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/branches-and-test-suite-review.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/182cfc16578fc599b151edb62e221722946c4a22/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/08/test-suite__branches-performance-quality-review.md>.*

---
# Branches check, test performance, test quality — 8 Oct 2026

*CLI team. Done as part of the 0.21.0 release.*

## 1. Branches: broken, now fixed and covered

An end-to-end check (create, list, switch in and out, work on a branch, push to it, pull from
it, merge either way) found that **branches did not work**: push, pull and fetch looked up the
named branch called `current` by name, so work committed on `feature` was pushed to main and the
feature ref never reached the server. Fixed, together with everything the check turned up behind
it (first push of a new branch, signing keys of new clone branches, switch dropping unpushed
commits and tripping a false rewind, switch not fetching, duplicate names, `--from` not checking
out, no way to merge a branch) and one bug that was not about branches at all: **every merge
commit a pull created was unsigned**, because the pull state carried the key id in a type that
turns `-` into `_`.

| | Where | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Unit, two real clones on the in-memory API | `tests/unit/review/test_Branches__End_To_End.py` | 22 |
| Integration, real SG/Send server | `tests/integration/test_Branches_Tags_Integrity__Integration.py` | 5 (branches, tags, format 2, signatures-required, rewind + lease) |
| Live dev API, through the CLI | manual run, two clones | create, push, switch, two people on one branch, diverged merge into main |

Why the existing tests missed it: the step tests for pull, push and fetch run against fake
branch managers whose `get_branch_by_name` returns the main branch whatever is asked; they
could not see work going to the wrong branch. The end-to-end tests run the real objects.

## 2. Performance: 70 s → 45 s, all 4,042 unit tests

| Change | Effect |
|---|---|
| Test vaults use a fixed key (`TEST_VAULT_KEY`) instead of a random one | Deriving a vault's keys is two PBKDF2 runs, ~190 ms by design. With one key, the process-level KDF cache makes every test vault after the first per worker nearly free. Each test still has its own directories and its own in-memory server |
| Test HTTP servers poll every 20 ms (static server 100 ms) | `shutdown()` waited up to 500 ms per test; 28 tests |
| Unit tests no longer reach the internet | 20 tests waited on the live dev server |

Checked and left: xdist scheduling (`load`/`loadscope`/`loadfile` within 2 s of each other),
collection (4 s), the vault-move test (22 real PBKDF2 runs is what a move does), two timing tests
whose subject is the timer itself (retry back-off, idle-socket age).

## 3. Quality

**Integration tests run real things.** All 12 files start the real SG/Send User Lambda on a
local port (in-memory storage) and nothing in them is mocked. They were all failing locally:
`mcp` 2.x breaks `fastapi-mcp` 0.4.0, which the server mounts at startup; CI pins `mcp<2`, the
local setup did not. Fixed in CLAUDE.md. 68 integration tests pass in 18 s.

**Unit tests are hermetic now.** `tests/unit/conftest.py` sends the default server to a closed
local port and fails, by name, any unit test that opens a connection to a non-loopback host.
Twenty were doing so: CLI commands on test vaults without a remote fell back to the live dev
server, one prompt test only passed because the live server answered, and `push`'s local dirty
check built a network client with no server. Production fixes for the last two.

**Where the mocking is.** It is concentrated, and it is the part of the suite that hid the
branch bug:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| unit test files | 335 (4,042 tests) |
| files that monkeypatch sgit_ai internals | 20 (258 patches) |
| files with hand-written Fake classes | 4 (37 classes) |
| tests named after a source line number | 82 |

Almost all of it is in files named `*__Coverage*`, written to reach lines rather than to check
behaviour. Recommendation, in order:

1. For new work, prefer the pattern the review tests use: real clones on the in-memory API
   (`Vault__Test_Env`), built once per class, restored per test (5 ms).
2. Replace the fake-based step tests (`test_Step__Pull/Push/Fetch__Coverage.py`) with workflow
   tests on real clones; delete the line-number tests whose behaviour another test already
   covers.
3. Treat a monkeypatch of an sgit_ai method in a unit test as a review flag: it usually means the
   code needs a seam (a parameter, a field) instead.

# Clone performance — the tree walk re-fetched shared sub-trees once per parent, cli.sgit.ai

> A clone stuck walking trees: the walk re-fetched shared sub-trees once per parent, 10,098 requests for 2,236 unique trees. The instrumented run and the fix.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/clone-refetched-shared-subtrees.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/182cfc16578fc599b151edb62e221722946c4a22/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/02/clone-performance__shared-subtree-refetch.md>.*

---
# Clone performance — the tree walk re-fetched shared sub-trees once per parent

**Date:** 2026-10-02
**Branch:** `claude/charming-babbage-5hzcxq` (from `dev` @ `0c9be4b`, v0.16.3)
**Vault probed:** `y8pwtjlw` (the DC collaboration vault, 172 commits at the time of the run)
**Reported with:** sgit-ai v0.14.27, stuck at `▸ Walking trees: obj-cas-imm-4c9e63979601`

## 1. What the clone was doing

An instrumented run of the real clone steps (derive keys → index → branch meta → walk
commits → walk trees) against the live vault, with the BFS tree walk mirrored exactly and
every batch request timed:

| phase            | time   | requests | notes                                                       |
|------------------|--------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| walk commits     | 32 s   | ~100     | linear chain: one commit per round trip                     |
| walk trees       | 377 s  | 205      | 10,098 tree ids requested for **2,236 unique** trees        |
| (blobs, not run) | ~15 s  | ~52      | 2,563 small blobs, fetched 8 chunks in parallel             |

The per-level picture of the tree walk is the whole story:

| level | queue | unique | duplication | requests | download |
|-------|-------|--------|-------------|----------|----------|
| 1     | 170   | 170    | 1.0×        | 4        | 7 s      |
| 2     | 2263  | 269    | **8.4×**    | 46       | 86 s     |
| 3     | 1938  | 508    | 3.8×        | 39       | 73 s     |
| 4     | 3561  | 811    | 4.4×        | 72       | 132 s    |
| 5     | 2135  | 460    | 4.6×        | 43       | 75 s     |
| 6     | 31    | 18     | 1.7×        | 1        | 1 s      |

Two defects compound:

1. **`Vault__Graph_Walk.walk_trees` queued a shared sub-tree once per parent.** `next_q`
   was only guarded by `sub not in visited`, and `visited` is updated at *processing* time,
   so within a level every root tree that pointed at the same unchanged folder enqueued
   its own copy. A 170-commit history whose root trees share most of their folders made
   the next level ~8× larger than it needed to be, and all of those duplicates went to
   `on_batch_missing` and so to the server. Nothing was written twice (the per-tree
   `visited` guard still held), but 4.5× the bytes and requests went over the wire.
2. **`Vault__API.batch_read` fetched its 50-id chunks one after another.** Each Lambda
   round trip costs ~1.7 s for 50 objects, so a 3,561-id level became 72 serial requests
   (132 s) during which the only progress line is the last *decrypted* tree id — which is
   why it looked hung on `obj-cas-imm-4c9e63979601`. The blob download step already fanned
   out 8 chunks in parallel; the tree walk did not.

The commit walk is a third, smaller cost: a linear chain needs one round trip per
commit because the parent id is inside the ciphertext. ~0.19 s per request × 172.

## 2. The fix (this branch)

- `Vault__Graph_Walk.walk_trees` keeps a `seen` set (queued ∪ visited) so every tree id is
  enqueued — and requested — exactly once. `on_batch_missing` still gets one call per BFS
  level. Pull's tree walk uses the same class and benefits identically.
- `Vault__API.batch_read` fans its chunks out over a bounded pool (`BATCH_READ_WORKERS = 8`,
  matching the blob fan-out); each chunk keeps its own 502 → per-file → presigned-S3
  fallback, and the first chunk failure still propagates as before. Single-chunk calls stay
  inline. `Vault__API__Static` already did this; `Vault__API__In_Memory` is unaffected.
- `Step__Clone__Walk_Trees` / `__Head_Only` emit `Walking trees: fetching N tree(s)` before
  each level's download so a large level is visible instead of looking stuck.

Measured on the same vault after the change, full `sgit clone`:

| phase    | before (probe)     | after        |
|----------|--------------------|--------------|
| commits  | 32 s               | 32 s         |
| trees    | 377 s              | **24 s**     |
| blobs    | ~15 s              | 14 s         |
| checkout | –                  | 0.4 s        |
| **wall** | **~7–8 min**       | **73 s**     |

`sgit check fsck` on the result reports 17 missing objects — all blobs, all also absent
on the server (`not_found` on a direct read), referenced by trees in commits
`7b72ec534ca6`, `3cd27e9b3222`, `ff4cc8df75e8`, `81c7fd7c6cb4`, `68797954d2ef` (several are
`*.conflict` files and `baseline.json`). That is a push from some client that never
uploaded those blobs; it is pre-existing and unrelated to the walker (the old walker's
probe store lacks them too). Worth noting: the blob step prints `2586 blobs` and does
not say that 17 came back empty — see §4.

Tests: 3 new walker tests (shared sub-tree requested once across 100 roots, duplicate
roots, one call per level) and 4 new `batch_read` tests (chunking + all returned, single
chunk inline, chunk failure propagates, 502 fallback confined to the failing chunk).
`pytest tests/unit/ -n auto` → **3841 passed**.

## 3. Would the newer releases have helped?

No. PyPI's latest is **0.16.0** (published 2026-08-20 from the last `dev → main` merge);
`dev` is at v0.16.3 but nothing after 0.16.0 has reached PyPI because publishing runs on
`main` only (`ci-pipeline__main.yml` sets `should_publish_pypi: true`; the dev pipeline
had publishing removed on 2026-08-14). Between 0.14.27 and today the walk code changed
once — the verify-before-write hook on 2026-08-20 — which does not touch the algorithm.
`Vault__Graph_Walk` itself was last edited 2026-05-11. So 0.16.0 clones this vault exactly
as slowly as 0.14.27; the fix needs a release that includes this branch.

The one `dev`-only change that *is* relevant to the follow-up question is `sgit vault
move` rewriting object ids (2026-08-20/21), which is also not on PyPI.

## 4. Follow-ups (not done here)

- **Commit walk round trips.** 172 serial requests at ~0.19 s. `curl` timing shows ~0.11 s
  of each ~0.43 s request is the TLS handshake (a reused connection answers in 0.16 s).
  `urllib.request.urlopen` opens a fresh connection per call; a per-thread persistent
  `http.client.HTTPSConnection` in `Vault__API._request` would roughly halve the commit
  walk and shave the tree/blob phases too. Needs care with proxies (`HTTPS_PROXY` is
  honoured by urllib today) and the retry path.
- **Silent missing blobs on clone.** `_download_blobs_by_id` drops `None` payloads
  without a word; the clone reports success and only `fsck` reveals the gap. A one-line
  `warning` with the count (and the first few file names, which the tree entries give)
  would have told the user about the 17 absent blobs at clone time.
- **`sgit check fsck` has the same per-commit re-walk**: it reported `44256 trees` for a
  vault with 2,264 unique trees because it restarts the tree walk from each commit with a
  fresh `visited_trees`. Local disk only, so it is seconds not minutes, but it scales
  with commits × tree size.
- **Full-clone shortcut**: a non-sparse clone downloads every reachable object anyway, so
  `list_files('bare/data/')` + one parallel bulk fetch + a local walk would collapse all
  three phases into one fan-out. It changes semantics (unreachable objects would be
  fetched too), so it is a design decision, not a patch.

## 5. Rekey while keeping history — where things stand

The brief's todo: *"a rekey loses the entire commit history"*. That is true of
`sgit vault rekey` (the `wipe` → `init` → `commit` flow: it deletes `.sg_vault/` and starts
a fresh history from the working tree). It is **not** true of `sgit vault move` on `dev`:

- `Step__Move__Build_Temp_Vault._rewrite_object_graph` classifies every object by
  reachability from the refs, then re-encrypts bottom-up — blobs, then trees with their
  `blob_id`/`tree_id` remapped and names re-encrypted deterministically, then commits with
  `tree_id` and `parents` remapped — storing each at its recomputed content address.
  Unreachable objects are carried too. Refs and the branch index are re-pointed.
- Verified locally on a throwaway vault (`init` + 3 commits): after the rewrite the new
  store under the new read key resolves the clone ref to a 4-commit chain
  (`commit 3 → commit 2 → commit 1 → init`) with the right file names at each step, 11
  objects in, 11 out, and **zero** shared ids between old and new store. Only the
  local build step was run (no access token in this session, so push/verify/delete-source
  were not exercised against the server).

So "rekey keeping history" already exists as `sgit vault move --new-key <key>`; the
hashes change (as expected) but the chain, messages and trees all survive. What it does
*not* do, and what the user may actually want:

- **Keep the same vault id.** `move` derives a new vault id from the new key, so it is a
  fork-and-delete, not an in-place rotation. Sharing links and `.sg_vault/local` configs on
  every clone go stale. An in-place variant would need the server to accept a full
  object-set replacement under the same id (write new objects, swap refs/index, delete
  old), and the read-key → ref-id derivation (`derive_ref_file_id(read_key, vault_id)`)
  means the named ref id changes with the key even if the vault id does not.
- **Ship it.** It is on `dev` only; PyPI 0.16.0 still has the old in-place re-encrypt
  that keeps ids (and therefore produces vaults that the new strict verify refuses).
- **`sgit vault rekey` should either delegate to `move` or say plainly that it discards
  history**, since today the two commands overlap in name and differ exactly on the point
  the brief cares about.

A full-chain check of `move` against the server (push → verify → clone the new key →
`history log` shows all commits) is the next thing to run, with a token.

---

## 6. Follow-up (same day): keep-alive connections — done, with a measurement caveat

Dinis asked for the connection-reuse follow-up without a new dependency. Implemented as
`sgit_ai/network/api/Vault__HTTP_Pool.py` (stdlib `http.client`) with `Vault__API._send`
on top; `_request` / `_request_bytes` keep their signatures and retry loop.

**Rules, as agreed, each with a test against a real local HTTP/1.1 keep-alive server
(`tests/unit/network/api/test_Vault__HTTP_Pool.py`, 21 tests):**

| rule | test |
|---|---|
| sequential calls share one socket; headers still sent per request; no `Connection: close` | `test_sequential_requests_share_one_connection`, `test_headers_still_sent_per_request` |
| server `Connection: close` honoured | `test_server_connection_close_is_honoured` |
| stale keep-alive → resend once, **reads only** (GET + batch read) | `test_stale_keep_alive_is_retried_for_idempotent_reads`, `test_batch_read_is_treated_as_idempotent` |
| stale keep-alive on a write → `URLError`, never replayed, pool recovers | `test_stale_keep_alive_never_resends_a_write` |
| failure on a *fresh* connection is not retried; half-read body poisons nothing | `test_fresh_connection_failure_is_not_retried` |
| same error text as before, token masked, connection reusable after a 4xx | `test_http_error_shape_and_body_preserved` |
| 502/503 retry loop unchanged, on the same connection | `test_transient_502_retries_then_succeeds_on_same_connection`, `…_exhausted…` |
| redirects not followed (token never replayed to another host) | `test_redirects_are_not_followed` |
| 8 threads × 5 calls → bounded pool, no errors | `test_parallel_callers_share_a_bounded_pool` |
| key = scheme/host/port/verify/proxy; `HTTPS_PROXY` → CONNECT tunnel with Basic auth; `NO_PROXY`; plain-http proxy → absolute URI | `Test_Vault__HTTP_Pool__Keys` |
| `SGIT_HTTP_NO_KEEPALIVE=1` → one connection per request (A/B switch) | `test_env_switch_disables_keep_alive` |

The pool is shared with a lock rather than thread-local on purpose: `batch_read` and the
blob download create a *new* `ThreadPoolExecutor` per call, so thread-local connections
would be discarded after every BFS level.

Other details: `User-Agent: sgit-ai` (the layer-import test forbids `network` importing
`_version`, so no version in it); the presigned-S3 fallback and the one-off `urlopen`
calls in doctor/static transport are untouched; `Vault__API.close()` drops the pool.

`pytest tests/unit/ -n auto` → **3861 passed** (one failure on the way: the layer-import
rule, fixed by dropping the version from the User-Agent).

**Measurement — read this before quoting numbers.** Every TLS connection from this
cloud session, including "direct" ones with `NO_PROXY=*`, is terminated by the session's
egress gateway (`openssl s_client` shows issuer `Egress Gateway SDS Issuing CA`, not
Amazon). So the numbers below describe *that* path, not a laptop talking to CloudFront:

| path | fresh connection per request (old) | reused (new) |
|---|---|---|
| via CONNECT proxy, 40 serial reads, mean | 388 / 340 ms | 292 / 283 ms |
| "direct" (still gateway-terminated), p50 | 217 / 185 ms | 327 / 329 ms |

The reused-connection path through the gateway is **bimodal**: ~145 ms or ~330 ms per
request, and `curl` shows exactly the same pattern on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 keep-alive, so
it is the gateway's upstream handling, not Python and not SG/Send (I ruled out client
delayed-ACK with `TCP_QUICKACK` and the two-segment request by sending headers+body in
one record — no change). Through the explicit proxy, where a fresh connection costs more,
keep-alive wins ~25 %. The full clone from here: `commits 27.4s  trees 36.3s  blobs 15.4s`
for 194 commits / 2,735 blobs (the vault grew by 22 commits during the session), wall 86 s.

On a laptop with no interception the expected saving is the handshake itself, which
Dinis can measure in one line (second number is the reused connection):

```
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'first=%{time_total}\n' https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/read/y8pwtjlw/bare/refs/x \
  --next -o /dev/null -w 'reused=%{time_total}\n' https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/read/y8pwtjlw/bare/refs/x
```

and for the real thing, the same clone twice: `sgit clone …` and
`SGIT_HTTP_NO_KEEPALIVE=1 sgit clone …`, comparing the `⏱ commits … trees … blobs …` line.

**Full-clone A/B from this session, same vault state (194 commits / 2,735 blobs), alternating:**

| run | keep-alive | commits (serial, 1 req each) | trees | blobs | wall |
|-----|-----------|------------------------------|-------|-------|------|
| 1   | on        | 27.3 s                       | 34.5 s | 14.9 s | 79 s |
| 2   | off       | 50.3 s                       | 27.1 s | 15.6 s | 96 s |
| 3   | on        | 26.8 s                       | 24.7 s | 13.7 s | 67 s |
| 4   | off       | 47.2 s                       | 26.4 s | 15.2 s | 91 s |

The serial commit walk — the phase that is one round trip per request — is where reuse
shows: 27 s vs 47–50 s. The parallel phases are within noise of each other (the
gateway's bimodal reused-connection latency cancels most of the handshake saving there).

---

## 7. Final review of the release PR (SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI#6) — findings and fixes

Ran the code-review pass at high effort over the three commits unique to this session (the
rest of `dev` was reviewed by the architecture sessions in August). Ten findings; what was
done with each:

| # | finding | verdict | action |
|---|---------|---------|--------|
| 1 | an idle connection the server has already closed could be handed to a **write** (push: ref read → long local encryption → batch POST), failing with `URLError` where urlopen's fresh socket succeeded | **real, the important one** | pool now checks liveness before reuse (`select` readable == FIN, or TLS bytes pending → drop) and never reuses a connection idle > 30 s (a NAT that forgot the mapping sends no FIN). Push gets a fresh socket after a long local phase, exactly as before |
| 2 | the stale-read resend re-acquired from the same idle bucket, so two stale sockets failed an idempotent read | real | the resend uses `acquire(fresh=True)`, bypassing the bucket |
| 3 | lazy pool creation raced when the first call was a parallel `batch_read` (8 threads → up to 8 pools, 7 orphaned) | real | double-checked lock around creation; test drives 8 chunks as the first call and asserts one pool holds every socket |
| 4 | plain `http://` base URL through an authenticated proxy never sent `Proxy-Authorization` | real, edge | `proxy_headers(key)` adds it per request on that path; the CONNECT path carries it on the tunnel as before; dead double-construction removed |
| 5 | a 3xx is now a hard failure with no explanation | real (UX) | `_api_error` adds a hint naming the `Location` and saying to set `--base-url` to the final https URL; wording avoids the 404/405/501 markers the auto transport looks for |
| 6 | `visited` included trees whose load failed (pre-existing) | real, pre-existing | with `seen` preventing re-enqueue the guard is unnecessary; `visited` is now "actually loaded", so `n_trees` is honest |
| 7 | dead code in `open_via_proxy` | cleanup | folded into #4 |
| 8 | three ad-hoc `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-outs (`batch_read`, static transport, clone blobs) | follow-up | not in this PR — a shared bounded fan-out helper is a refactor, not a fix |
| 9 | the four `batch_read` tests used `unittest.mock.patch` (CLAUDE.md: no mocks) | real | rewritten against the local keep-alive server, which now has a real batch endpoint (base64 of the file id; scripted 502 for one chunk) |
| 10 | `object`-typed pool fields | convention | `timeout_seconds` / `max_idle_seconds` are `Safe_UInt`; the socket bookkeeping (`idle`, `warm`, `lock`) stays `object`, the same pattern as `Clone__Workspace`'s managers |

Also added while here: every pooled socket has a 120 s per-operation timeout (urlopen had
none; a kept-alive socket is the one place a silent peer can hang a command forever).

One pre-existing behaviour the 502 test made visible, left alone: a 502 from the batch
endpoint (Lambda response-size limit) is first retried whole three times with 2 + 4 + 8 s
of sleeping before `batch_read` falls back to per-file reads. For a *size*-caused 502 the
retries can never succeed; skipping them would save 14 s on that path.

Suite after the fixes: `pytest tests/unit/ -n auto` → **3871 passed**.
