# Response: "sgit-ai 0.25.0 in the newsroom, first morning" (conductor@php.newsroom, 26 Oct 2026)

**Brief:** `2026-10-26__brief__for-the-sgit-cli-team-0-25-0-in-the-newsroom.md`.
**In one line:** items 1, 3 and 5 are fixed on the branch (the first command after a fresh clone no longer reads
the files it just wrote; `sgit version` names a shadowing install); item 2, the pull of a whole pass, is measured
below with where the time goes and what is fixed now versus next; item 4 needs nothing.

## 1. The first `status` after a clone (items 1 and 3)

**What it was doing.** Exactly what the brief suspected: reading every file's content where a stat would do. The
scan cache (0.25.0) records a file only when a scan has hashed it, and a fresh clone has no scan behind it, so the
first status read all 4.2 GB back from the session's scratch disk. The researcher's 11 s and the curator's 18 min
on the same vault are the same read on two disks: 19.6 s user + 41.5 s sys is the hashing and the syscalls; the
17 minutes between is the disk. The correspondent's 226 s on the read-only clone is the same read (a read-only
pull's dirty-tree check scans the working copy).

**What changed.** sgit wrote those files itself, so it knows their hashes. Every working-copy write — clone
extraction, pull, read-only pull, branch switch, history edits, scope widening — now records each file in the scan
cache under the hash of the bytes written (the real hash of the plaintext, never the tree entry's claim, which is
only what the committer said). The next status, commit or pull stats the file and moves on. Two details:

- the racy rule still holds: a scan that starts within two seconds of the write reads the file, and keeps the
  record when the hash it computes is the recorded one, so a status immediately after a clone is not the one
  that throws the seed away;
- a full clone now extracts through the flat map and writes the head's flat cache, so that first status opens
  no tree either (the tree walk through the schema was the other half of the researcher's 11 s).

**Measured** on the synthetic vault (228,000 files, 305,230 objects, in-memory host, a fast local disk):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| clone | 275 s | 216 s |
| first `status` after the clone | 20.1 s (every file read and hashed) | 8.2 s |
| second `status` | 7.4 s | 6.5 s |

Here the disk is fast, so "before" is the hashing; on the curator's session it was the 18 minutes. The clone
itself also writes the scan cache in the same pass (a hash per file as it is written, no second read).

**Lazily or in the background?** Not needed once the seed exists, and a lazy build would be wrong: a status
must know whether a file changed, and only a hash (or a record of what sgit wrote) can say so. The one case left
is a clone made by 0.24.x or 0.25.0 and then upgraded: its first status still reads everything once. Agents on
fresh containers never hit that.

## 2. The pull of a whole pass (item 2)

**Measured** on the synthetic vault (228,000 files), a 300-file pass pushed from one clone and pulled in another,
under cProfile: **566 s before, 31.7 s after.** Where the 566 s went, and what changed:

| Cost | Before | Cause | Now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the fetch's tree walk | 347 s (154,454 tree loads through `Type_Safe.from_json`) | every tree of the new head was opened to find what was missing, twice | the walk does not open a folder of the head this clone last accepted (that record is written only once every object of the head was local), and the trees it does open are read as JSON: 8 trees opened for a two-leaf change on a 24-tree test vault |
| writing the working copy | 171 s (229,310 files written for 301 changed) | the merge checked out the whole merged tree | only the files whose blob changed are written |
| flattening the new head | ~45 s | a full walk, the cache being for the old head | the new head's map is built by copying the unchanged folders from the cached old head |

What is left in the 31.7 s is the vault's size, in seconds: the dirty-tree scan (15 s, one `lstat` per file over
228k files), the missing-blob check (6 s, `exists` over 235k ids) and pruning empty folders after deletes (5 s).
On the curator's clone, the 8 minutes also held the disk writes of 6,807 files, which stay.

## 3. `sgit version` and a shadowing install (item 5)

`sgit version` now prints a note when the `sgit` first on the PATH is another program, with that one's version
when it answers:

```
sgit-ai 0.25.1
note: the `sgit` first on your PATH is /usr/local/bin/sgit (sgit-ai 0.24.0), not this one
      (/home/agent/.venv/bin/sgit). Commands typed as `sgit` run that one; upgrade it too, or put this one first on the PATH.
```

It compares the resolved paths and, failing that, the entry scripts' bytes, so a venv's `sgit` and the same
script reached through another path are not reported as two installs. Only `sgit version` checks (every command
would cost a PATH search and a subprocess per invocation); the wake step that runs `sgit version` first gets it.

## 4. Commit and push (item 4)

Nothing to do: 25 s and 67 s for phase 1 of a pass on 79,000 files, 4 s and 16 s for phase 2, are the branch
working as intended, and the 35-minute pass is the capture. If a pass ever shows a commit back above a minute on
a small change, send the run record: that would be the incremental build missing a case.

## 5. Files

`sgit_ai/core/Vault__Sync__Base.py` (`_checkout_flat_map` seeds; `_scan_cache_seed`; a confirmed seed survives a
racy scan), `sgit_ai/workflow/clone/Step__Clone__Extract_Working_Copy.py` (flat-map extraction, flat cache
written, a refused tree still refuses the clone), `sgit_ai/storage/Vault__Sub_Tree.py` (the flat cache is written
through to a vault that has none), `sgit_ai/cli/CLI__Main.py` (`cmd_version`, `path_shadow_note`). Tests:
`tests/unit/sync/test_Vault__Sync__Scan_Cache__Seeded_On_Write.py`, `tests/unit/cli/test_CLI__Version__Path_Note.py`.

# AC-L-001 / TM-R36 — characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9/\_.- ]` in paths: what really happens, cli.sgit.ai

> Characters outside a narrow set in a path are silently rewritten, so one vault gets two roots and a false push conflict. What really happens, reproduced, and a fix that raises an alarm instead of rewriting.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/non-ascii-paths-refuse-dont-rewrite.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/182cfc16578fc599b151edb62e221722946c4a22/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/13/AC-L-001__non-ascii-paths__refuse-dont-rewrite.md>.*

---
# AC-L-001 / TM-R36 — characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9/\_.- ]` in paths: what really happens

**Status:** documented, **not fixed in this push** (your call, 13 Oct). Reproduced on `dev` at
81a4176 with the Python API over the in-memory host. The fix proposal below follows your
instinct: **raise an alarm, never rewrite silently**. It is narrower than "refuse every such
character", for the reason in §3.

It is worse than the round-1 record (`review/findings/audit-context-local.json` AC-L-001) says.
Two different things share the bug: **where the vault lives** (the host path of the clone) and
**names inside the vault** (file and folder names in the trees).

## 1. The vault root: broken, and silently in the wrong place

`Safe_Str__Vault_Path` and `Safe_Str__File_Path` both use `[^a-zA-Z0-9/\\_.\- ]` in *replace*
mode: every other character becomes `_`. The working directory of the clone, pull, fetch,
push and move workflows (`directory : Safe_Str__File_Path`), `Vault__Context.vault_path` and
`Vault__Storage` go through them; other code uses the raw `str`. So one vault gets two roots.

| Step, under `/tmp/x/josé/vault` | What happened |
|---|---|
| `init` | the working copy and `.sg_vault/{bare,local}` are under `josé/vault`, **and** a second tree `jos_/vault/` is created next to it |
| `commit`, `status` | ok, `clean` |
| first `push` | **`Vault__Push_Conflict_Error`: "the branch moved on the server while this push was in flight"** — false; nothing was pushed |
| `clone` into `josé/clone` | reports success; **the whole clone is written to `jos_/clone`**; `josé/clone` does not exist |
| `pull` in `josé/clone` | `FileNotFoundError: …/josé/clone/.sg_vault/local/vault_key` |
| second `commit` + `push` in `josé/vault` | `FileNotFoundError: …/jos_/vault/.sg_vault/work/pull-…/.tmp-…` |

It is not only accents. What the type does to real folder names:

| Path | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `/Users/x/Dropbox (Personal)/v` | `/Users/x/Dropbox _Personal_/v` |
| `/Users/x/OneDrive - Acme, Inc/v` | `/Users/x/OneDrive - Acme_ Inc/v` |
| `/home/first.last@corp/v` | `/home/first.last_corp/v` |
| `/home/u/my+vault` | `/home/u/my_vault` |
| `C:\Users\Zoë\v` | `C_\Users\Zo_\v` |

**The last row needs a check on Windows.** The colon of every drive letter is rewritten, so if
any of these fields carries an absolute Windows path, every Windows user is affected, not just
users with accented names. I could not run Windows here.

Security reading: a write lands in a directory the user never named. Two roots that sanitise
alike share one store (`josé/` and `josè/` and a real `jos_/`), so one vault's objects, refs and
`work/` files can mix with another's. A local process (A6) that can create `jos_/` next to
`josé/` decides where the store goes. Likelihood M (any European or company folder name, any
Dropbox or OneDrive folder); impact H (a false "conflict", a clone in the wrong place, failures
on the next command). I have raised TM-R36 from M / M to M / H.

## 2. Names inside the vault: the core is right; the display and `--path` are not

Tree entry names are encrypted strings, not `Safe_Str` fields, so the sync path never touches
them. With `café.md`, `naïve dir/résumé.md`, `a+b@c.md`, `日本語.txt` and a `caf_.md` beside
`café.md`:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| status, commit, push, clone | every file round-trips byte for byte, with the exact name; `café.md` and `caf_.md` stay two files |
| edit in the clone, push, pull in the first clone | ok; content and name exact |
| `stash` / `stash pop` | ok |
| **`sgit diff`** (`Schema__Diff_File.path`) | **lists `caf_.md` and `na_ve/r_sum_.md`**: the display lies |
| **`sgit clone --path naïve`** (`scope_paths : list[Safe_Str__File_Path]`) | **records the scope `na_ve`, checks out nothing, and says nothing** |
| history file lists, publish entries, stash metadata | typed with the same class, so they rewrite the same way (not each one run) |

So "what happens if the vault creates that": another client, or the web UI, can put such a
name in a vault. This CLI clones, edits and syncs it correctly. Its listings show the wrong
name, and a scoped clone of that folder is silently empty.

Hostile names in a vault are a separate question with an existing answer: `Vault__Path_Guard`
refuses absolute paths, `..` on either separator, `.git` / `.sg_vault`, and writes through a
symlink at checkout (TM-F series). Nothing in this finding weakens that.

## 3. The decision proposed for the next push

**The rule:** a type that names a place must **refuse** what it cannot represent, never rewrite
it. A rewritten path is a silent data change: the user asked for one place and got another.
Worth a line in CLAUDE.md's Type_Safe rules.

1. **Vault roots: the alarm now, the real fix right behind it.**
   - *Stop-gap (S):* at the CLI boundary, before any command uses a vault root (`init`, `clone*`,
     and resolving the root of every other command), refuse a root the type would change:
     > `sgit cannot work in a folder whose path contains 'é' (…/josé/vault) yet. Move the vault, or clone it, to a path made of letters a-z, digits, space, '.', '_' and '-'. (TM-R36)`
   - *Fix (M):* type the host-side fields (`directory`, `vault_path`, the storage root) with
     `Safe_Str__Host_Path`. It already exists, added for `sgit serve`: any printable text,
     control characters refused, never rewritten. Then the alarm is no longer needed.
2. **Names inside a vault: do not refuse them.** They work today, other clients create them,
   and refusing would lock people out of their own vaults. That is the lock-out lesson of R1 and
   TM-F35. Instead:
   - a content-path type (Unicode allowed; NUL, control characters, absolute paths and `..`
     refused) for the display and scope schemas: `Schema__Diff_File`, history lists,
     `scope_paths`, publish entries, stash metadata;
   - `clone --path` refuses a folder that is not in the tree, rather than cloning nothing.
3. **Where an alarm is right for content: names that will not survive another OS.** Add a check
   (rule 9 puts it under `check`), and a warning at `commit` time for new names only (an alarm,
   not a refusal). It covers:
   - case-only collisions (`A.md` and `a.md` are one file on macOS and Windows);
   - Unicode normalisation twins (NFC and NFD `café`; macOS can hand back the other form, so
     status shows a delete and an add);
   - Windows-reserved names (`CON`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`…, a trailing dot or space, `<>:"|?*`);
   - control characters and newlines;
   - paths too long for Windows.
4. **Tests that land with the fix:**
   - init, commit, push, clone and pull under a root with `é`, `+`, `@`, `(` and a space;
   - clone into `josé/`;
   - `clone --path naïve`;
   - `diff` listing the exact names;
   - a `Fixed` security test that two roots that used to sanitise alike no longer share a store;
   - the check's cases.

Sizes: the stop-gap is under a day. The type change is a day or two, because the type is used by
every path field; the check is about a day.

## Where this is recorded

- Threat model TM-R36: likelihood/impact raised, this evidence linked.
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → "Known issue".
- Probe scripts were run from the session scratchpad. Their steps are in the tables above.

# Architecture: the pack as the store, and the indexes it carries, cli.sgit.ai

> The CLI team's exploration after the 0.25.0 field report: keep the packs a clone downloads and read objects in place; carry flat, diff and graph indexes inside the pack, encrypted under the read key and signed by the pusher; assemble them locally into SQLite; four phases. Nothing in it is built.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/pack-carried-indexes-architecture.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/c06947537e3927c82578307b62434bc0901952c5/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/26/architecture__pack-resident-store-and-pack-carried-indexes.md>.*

# Architecture: the pack as the store, and the indexes it carries

**Status:** exploration, 26 Oct 2026, from the brief after the 0.25.0 field report ("ship the indexes in the zip,
assemble them locally, don't extract the files"). Nothing here is built; section 9 says what to build first.
**Builds on:** [`review__indexes-and-caches-across-the-board.md`](../research/indexes-and-caches-review.md) (same folder), pack mode (0.24.0), the local
caches (0.25.0), the cache layer (contract 08/12).

## 0. The idea, and why it works now when it did not in August

The August objection to indexes was right twice over: an index is one more file per thing indexed, on a host
where every file is a request; and an index that describes mutable state has to be maintained, which is more
requests, by every writer, racing. The cache layer (08/12) survived that by being per path, derived, optional
and repairable, and it stayed small.

A pack changes both terms. A pack is immutable: one zip per push, named by its commit, never rewritten, replaced
only by compaction. Anything derived from the objects in it is as immutable as the pack and can travel inside
it: no extra request, no maintenance, no race, written once by the one client that already holds the answer
(the pusher) and read by everyone who downloads the pack anyway. The index is not a file on the host that
someone keeps current; it is a member of a thing that is never current, only complete.

And the second half of the brief follows from the first: if the pack carries what a reader needs to know
*about* its objects, the reader does not need to take the objects *out* of it. The pack can be the store.

Two numbers from this week say why that matters. A clone of the synthetic vault writes 305,230 objects
(1.2 GB) into `bare/data/` and then 228,000 working files: 216 to 288 s here, and on a cloud session's disk the
curator's first command afterwards waited 17 minutes on that disk. Nearly every one of those object writes is
a copy of bytes the clone already holds, contiguously, in the one file it downloaded.

## 1. What is authoritative, what is derived, what the host may see

The design rests on the distinction sgit has kept since the start:

| | Authoritative | Derived |
|---|---|---|
| what | blobs, trees, commits (`obj-cas-imm-*`, content-addressed), refs, the branch index, keys | everything computable from those plus a key: flat maps, folder ids, diffs, graph shortcuts, the scan state, object locations |
| may be lost? | no | yes: rebuilt from the authoritative set; the rebuild is the only cost |
| trusted? | by content address (blobs, trees), by signature (commits), by CAS (refs) | never for correctness: checked against the authoritative object it claims to describe, or used only to plan |

Everything in this document is in the right-hand column, with one rule added: **a derived object may decide
what to fetch, what to open and what to write, but nothing is written to the working copy or to the store
unless the authoritative object it came from verified.** That is already how packs work (a member is verified
by its content address before it is written); the same rule carries over when the member is read in place.

What the host may see does not change. It already sees: pack names (epoch, commit id, bytes), each pack's
central directory (object ids and ciphertext sizes), the commit graph's shape through pack names, and every
ref. It never sees a path name, a file's content, a message, or which object is a tree. An index member must
keep that boundary: **ids and sizes may be clear; names, paths and relations between named things are
encrypted under the read key** like a tree is. The thing "everything is a hash" buys is that the clear part of
an index can be the join key, and the encrypted part the payload.

## 2. The pack as the store

### 2.1 Today

`sync_down` downloads a pack to memory, checks each member (stored uncompressed, name is an object id, size
matches), verifies it by content address, writes it loose under `.sg_vault/bare/data/`, and discards the zip.
The local store is always loose; `bare/packs/` exists only on the host.

### 2.2 Proposed

The clone keeps the packs it downloads under `.sg_vault/bare/packs/` (the host's names), and the object store
answers a read from either place:

1. loose, `bare/data/<id>` (objects this clone made and has not pushed; anything older code wrote);
2. packed: a local **pack index** maps `<id> -> (pack file, offset, length)`; a read is one `seek` and one
   `read` of `length` bytes (members are `ZIP_STORED`, so the bytes in the file are the ciphertext itself;
   blob deflate is inside the ciphertext, not the zip).

The pack index is derived from the zip central directories (one pass per pack when it arrives, ~1 ms per
thousand members), kept as a local file, and losable: a missing or corrupt index is rebuilt by re-reading the
central directories of the packs on disk.

Verification moves from write time to the first read of each object: the bytes read from the pack are hashed
against the id before they are used, and the verdict is remembered (a bit per object in the pack index). The
first clone of a 305k-object vault no longer hashes 305k objects before anyone can work; it hashes what it
reads, and `sgit check fsck` hashes everything.

What changes for each writer of the store:

- **push** already builds the commit pack from the loose objects of the pushed commits; after a successful push
  it keeps that pack locally and may drop the loose copies (or keep both until the next compaction; loose
  wins on a read, so correctness does not depend on the choice).
- **compaction** already replaces commit packs with a snapshot on the host; locally it does the same: a
  snapshot that arrives supersedes the packs it absorbed, which are removed once the new index covers them.
- **`vault move`**, `pack import/export`, `history` edits and `uninit`'s backup read through the same store
  API and need nothing new.
- the **three invariants** of the pack layer stand: a member is only ever `bare/data/<object id>`, stored,
  unique, and refused whole on any violation; nothing in a pack is trusted before its content address checks.

Working-copy extraction becomes a streaming read: for each entry of the head's flat map, read the blob's bytes
from the pack at its offset, decrypt, write the file, seed the scan cache. The 305k object writes disappear;
the 228k file writes remain (they are the working copy).

### 2.3 Costs and risks

- One open file handle per pack during a command (a handful; compaction keeps it a handful).
- A pack on a cloud disk is one large file: a partial download must be detected (size from the listing name,
  and the zip end-of-central-directory) before it is indexed; today's "verify before write" becomes "verify
  before index".
- Windows: a pack held open cannot be replaced; compaction's local swap must close handles first (the same
  rule `vault move` follows for `.sg_vault`).
- Zip64 for packs over 4 GB: the writer already sets `allowZip64`; the reader must index 64-bit offsets.
- A loose object and a packed one with the same id are the same bytes by definition; `fsck` reports a
  disagreement as corruption of whichever fails its hash.

## 3. What a pack carries besides objects

Each member below is one file inside the zip, under a reserved prefix (`bare/index/`), encrypted under the
read key with AES-GCM like a tree, and named by the authoritative object it describes, so it is immutable and
needs no version of its own. Readers that predate the feature refuse the pack (section 7).

| Member | Describes | Content (plaintext, before encryption) | Written by | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`flat/<tree id>`** | one head | every path with blob id, size, content hash, content type; every folder path with its tree id | the pusher, from its flat cache | the clone's and pull's fetch plan; the first flatten; a keyed reader's "where is this file" |
| **`diff/<commit id>`** | one commit | added, modified, deleted paths with old and new blob ids | the pusher (it computed it to build the pack) | `history log`, `pull`'s commit lines, "what did this pass change", the merge's apply map |
| **`graph/<commit id>`** | one commit | parents, timestamp, tree id, author key id, and the commit's generation number | the pusher | ancestry walks without opening commits; an exact `base..head` and merge base for any clock |
| **`manifest`** (clear) | the pack | the member ids and sizes | the zip's own central directory, already present | the pack index; nothing new to write |

Sizes on the newsroom's vault: the flat index of a 79,465-file head is ~12 MB as compact JSON, ~2 MB
deflated; a diff is proportional to the pass (hundreds of KB); a graph entry is bytes. Against a 1.22 GB
snapshot and 164 to 228 MB commit packs, the indexes are noise, and they go through the same batch write.

**Signature.** The flat and diff members are signed by the pusher's clone key over (the id they describe,
sha256 of the plaintext), as a commit is signed, and accepted on the same policy as the commit that names their
tree. Without that, a write-key holder could ship a map that disagrees with the trees and bypass the signature
the trees enjoy through their commit. With it, the index has exactly the standing of the commit, and a reader
that does not trust unsigned commits does not trust unsigned indexes either.

**Not carried.** Scan state (this machine's inodes and mtimes) and object presence (this clone's store) are
local by nature. Application indexes (what a newsroom builds over its sources) are ordinary vault content.

## 4. The local assembly: from members to a database

A pack delivers the indexes as members; the clone **assembles** them into whatever local form answers its
questions fastest. This is the load, extract, transform, save step, done once per pack, locally, where it is
cheap, by the one process that just downloaded the pack.

The natural target is SQLite (in the standard library, transactional, one file), as the local materialisation
of the pack indexes; a graph store over the commit graph is the same data with a different index. Either way,
the assembled database is a **cache with a well-known shape**, under `.sg_vault/local/`, losable, and rebuilt
from the packs on disk.

| Table | Rows | Fed by | Answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objects(id, pack, offset, length, verified)` | one per member | every pack's central directory | "where are the bytes of X"; fsck |
| `flat(tree, path, blob, size, hash, type)` | one per file per head kept (the newest two heads) | `flat/<tree>` | status, commit's incremental build, cat, fetch, "which file is where" |
| `folders(tree, path, child_tree)` | one per folder per head kept | `flat/<tree>` | the incremental build's reuse; the fetch plan (which folders changed) |
| `commits(id, parent, ts, tree, generation)` | one per commit | `graph/<commit>` | log, pull's list, merge base, rewind guard |
| `changes(commit, path, kind, old_blob, new_blob)` | one per changed path per commit | `diff/<commit>` | `history log --stat`, "what did this pass change", blame-like queries |
| `scan(path, mtime, ctime, size, ino, dev, hash)` | one per working file | the scan (local) | status without reading |

With this, the commands the newsroom runs every wake are a stat pass plus SQL: `status` is `scan` against
`flat` for the head; `commit` is the incremental build with reuse decided from `folders`; `pull` of N packs is
N index loads plus a diff-sized set of file writes; `history log` is a query; "where is this file" is a row
lookup and one seek into a pack.

**What stays plaintext locally.** Path names, sizes, hashes, messages: the same set the 0.25.0 caches hold
(TM-R41), in the same folder as `vault_key`. Under the sealed-vault-keys design this database must be either
encrypted at rest (SQLCipher, or the file encrypted under a key derived from the read key and opened to a
memory database per command) or memory-only, assembled from the packs on each run; the second is slower but
needs nothing new. Decide when sealed keys land.

## 5. Why the files need not be extracted

With sections 2 to 4 in place, "extract" means two different things, and only one is still needed:

- the **store** need never be extracted: the object store reads members in place;
- the **working copy** is extracted only because that is what a working copy is: files on disk for the user's
  tools. A clone that is only read (a research reader, a Lambda, SG/Vault, a pipeline that feeds its own
  database) can skip it entirely and read blobs through the index: `sgit cat` and `sgit fetch <path>` become
  one row lookup and one seek, no working copy at all. That is the "bare" clone with an index, and it is the
  shape most agents in the newsroom actually need between passes.

And a reader without any clone: the flat index of the head is one object, the pack's central directory tells
where each blob sits, and `fetch_presigned_range` already exists. "Give me this file from this vault" is one
read of the index member and one ranged read of the member's bytes, from the host, no clone, no walk. That is
the cache layer's one-request read generalised to every path of a pack vault.

## 6. What the brief says, checked against this

- *"Already provide the indexes in the zip."* Yes: section 3; one encryption and one member per index at push.
- *"Assembled locally, high performance, local databases."* Yes: section 4; SQLite first, a graph store on the
  same rows when a question needs it.
- *"Because we can encrypt the data again, this scales."* Yes, with the boundary of section 1: ids and sizes
  in clear, names and relations encrypted on the host; locally, whatever the sealed-keys decision says.
- *"Rearrange the files locally so you know exactly what you are consuming."* That is the pack index and the
  `objects` table: the clone knows, per object, which pack holds it and whether it verified.
- *"I would not even need to extract the files."* The store: never. The working copy: only for a working clone;
  a reading agent needs none (section 5).
- *"Everything is a hash, so some values can be clear."* The join keys can be clear everywhere, including on
  the host, because they are content addresses that already appear in pack directories; what must stay
  encrypted is what relates a key to a name.

One thing the brief does not say and this design must: the index is a plan, never a proof. A member read from
a pack is still verified by its address before it is used; a signed index that disagrees with its tree is the
signer's fault and is refused like a bad commit; an unsigned index on a vault that requires signatures is
ignored and the walk happens. Lose every index and nothing is lost; trust an index and nothing is written
unverified.

## 7. Format, compatibility, rollout

- Two features in the branch index, each with its min client, gated exactly like `packs` and `blob-deflate`
  (`FEATURE_MIN_CLIENT`, `gate_this_build_carries`): `pack-index` (packs carry `bare/index/*` members) and
  `pack-store` (clones may keep packs in place). A 0.24.x or 0.25.0 client refuses a pack with an index member
  whole (the member rule), so `pack-index` is a gate, not a hint. `pack-store` is local-only behaviour and
  gates nothing on the host; it is a feature so that a vault can say "its clones are expected to hold packs".
- Compaction writes the snapshot's `flat/<head tree>` and the graph members for every commit it absorbs; that
  is how an existing pack vault gains indexes without a re-push: one `sgit pack compact` by an upgraded client.
- `pack import` (loose to pack) writes them too; `pack export` ignores them.
- The local database is versioned by a schema number in its one metadata row; a mismatch drops and rebuilds.

## 8. Risks and open questions

1. **Reading through packs on slow disks** trades many small writes for seeks into one large file. On a
   cloud session's scratch disk that is the right trade (sequential download, random reads of what is used);
   measure it on the newsroom's session before making `pack-store` the default.
2. **The flat index duplicates what the trees say.** By design, like every index; the signature and the root
   check keep it honest, and `fsck --indexes` can compare a flat member to its trees in full.
3. **How much to keep in SQLite versus JSON files.** The 0.25.0 caches are JSON and they are enough for the
   per-head questions; the database pays off when questions cross heads and commits (log, blame, "what changed
   since"). Start with JSON members in the pack and SQLite as the local assembly; the members' format does not
   change if the local form does.
4. **Memory-only versus on-disk database under sealed keys.** Deferred to that design; nothing here forecloses
   either.
5. **Generation numbers** in `graph/` make `base..head` exact for any clock; the day-window walk on the branch
   is the interim.

## 9. Order of work

| Phase | What | Removes | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pack-store`: packs kept locally, pack index, object store reads in place, verify-on-first-read, streaming extraction, fsck over packs, compaction's local swap | the 305k object writes of a clone; the disk wait behind the first command | 3 days |
| 2 | `pack-index`: `flat/<tree>` and `graph/<commit>` members written at push and compaction, signed; the fetch plan from two flat maps; the first flatten from the member | the last tree walks (clone, pull of an unseen head); one-request reads for keyed readers | 3 days |
| 3 | `diff/<commit>` and the local SQLite assembly (`objects`, `flat`, `folders`, `commits`, `changes`) | per-commit questions as queries; the index-only (bare) reader | 3 days |
| 4 | the remote one-request path (index member + ranged member read) in `sgit cat` / `fetch` without a clone, and in SG/Vault | the clone itself, for readers | with the SG/Vault team |

Phase 1 is self-contained and measurable on the newsroom's own session (the curator's 18 minutes is its
benchmark); phase 2 needs the gate and is where the brief's idea lands; phase 3 is where the local database
earns its keep; phase 4 is the payoff for readers.

# Review: the pack-indexes branch — quality, security, and side effects on 0.25.0 vaults (26 Oct 2026), cli.sgit.ai

# Review: the pack-indexes branch — quality, security, and side effects on 0.25.0 vaults (26 Oct 2026)

**Scope:** `c3f410ba..a9f24d8` on `claude/charming-babbage-5hzcxq` (56 source files, +3,494 / −168), the seven
commits since 0.25.0. **Method:** three independent reviewers (security; compatibility with 0.25.0 clients and
vaults; correctness of pull, checkout and pack store), each given the code and not my conclusions, each
proving findings with scripts; plus a cross-version run against the real SG/Send test server with the released
`sgit-ai==0.25.0` from PyPI and the branch build, in three shared-vault scenarios. Every finding below was
re-run by me. Nothing was fixed yet: this is the assessment.

## 1. Side effects on 0.25.0 vaults and clients: none breaking, four to know about

The cross-version run (server at `sgraph-ai-app-send`, `tests/integration`'s fixture, in-memory storage):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| A. a pack vault the new client made and pushed; 0.25.0 clones, pulls, pushes; the new client compacts; 0.25.0 pulls, verifies, pushes again; a fresh 0.25.0 clone after compaction | every command OK; trees identical at every hop; `pack verify` ok on path-ordered packs |
| B. a pack vault only 0.25.0 wrote; the new client clones (full, `--no-checkout`, `--pack-store`, `--path`), pulls, pushes, runs `pack index build`; 0.25.0 pulls and verifies between | every command OK; trees identical |
| C. a loose vault shared by both, interleaved commits and pulls | every command OK; trees identical |

Why nothing breaks, with the code: 0.25.0 never lists `bare/packs/indexes/` (its `list_folder` filters on
`commits/` and `snapshots/`); it ignores the unknown feature `pack-indexes` (`Vault__Format.check_client`
returns once the build is at or above `min_client`, and no `FEATURE_MIN_CLIENT` entry raises the gate);
extraction and `pack verify` do not depend on member order; the pack name regex, `packs_absorbed.json`,
`remote_heads.json`, flat-cache v2 and scan-cache v2 are unchanged; `Schema__Local_Config.from_json` ignores
the new `pack_store` key, so 0.25.0 reads a config the new client wrote.

The side effects that are real:

| # | Population | Effect | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 0.25.0 **sparse** clones (loose vaults) | `sgit fetch` with no path, or `--all`, now goes through `checkout --all`, which clears the sparse flag and removes the record: the clone becomes full, and on-disk absences become deletions at the next commit. 0.25.0's `sparse_fetch` never flipped the flag. | Medium: a semantic change on an existing clone type |
| S2 | any pack vault, old or new | every push by the new client uploads an index pack beside its data pack (one more batch write, at least 16 KiB each because the header is padded), feature or not; on a 0.25.0-created vault nobody reads them until `sgit pack index build` runs, which also writes the `pack-indexes` feature into the branch index (a CAS write other clones may contend with) | Low: host bytes and one write per push |
| S3 | `sgit dump` (both versions) | takes every file under `bare/packs/indexes/` for a branch index (`'/indexes/' in f`) and reports a decrypt error per index pack; the dump is otherwise fine | Medium as noise in a check tool |
| S4 | 0.25.0 compaction of a vault with index packs | 0.25.0 does not move index packs to `indexes/archive/`, so orphans accumulate; the new client only reports them (`pack index verify` → orphans); the docstring's "deleted by the next run" is not implemented | Low |
| S5 | request counts (pack vaults) | push: 3 batch writes instead of 2; pull with new packs: 3 listings instead of 2 (0 extra when up to date); fresh clone: 4 listings instead of 2; compaction: about three more listings per moved pack. A scoped clone's ranged reads cost two requests per range (the presigned URL is fetched per `read_range`) and two per pack for the directory; `sgit serve` and memory hosts answer 400 and the client falls back to whole packs after one failed call | Low; Medium for scoped clones on S3 hosts |
| S6 | branch builds | the branch's `sgit_ai/version` says 0.24.3 (the pipeline bumps it on dev), so a vault **created by 0.25.0** refuses the branch build by its own gate (`min_client = max(build, 0.24.0)` at init). The merge fixes it; until then test against 0.25.0-created vaults with the version file set | Info |

Also worth knowing: a `--pack-store` clone must not be opened by 0.25.0 (its `bare/data/` is empty: 0.25.0 would
refetch); the status line `Sparse mode: n/m file(s) fetched locally` is now `Selective working copy: n/m
tracked file(s) checked out` (JSON keys unchanged); `sgit checkout main` out of git habit prints "not a tracked
file" and exits 1 (`sgit branch checkout` switches); every new flag defaults off.

## 2. Findings in the new code (ranked)

| # | Severity | Where | What | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **High** (data loss) | `Vault__Sync__Checkout.checkout`, `:42-43` | `checkout --all` calls `_make_full` even when blobs failed to download (`missing` non-empty): the clone becomes full, status shows those files deleted, the next commit of anything else deletes them from the vault for everyone. Proven on a loose sparse clone with one blob removed from the host. | call `_make_full` only when `not missing`; otherwise refuse as the clone's `_refuse_incomplete` does |
| F2 | **High** (data loss) | `Vault__Sync__Checkout.checkout`, `:40` | `checkout <path>`, `--all`, `--changed-since` and `fetch <path>` overwrite an uncommitted edit with HEAD, no warning (the pull has `Vault__Pull__Guard`; this path has nothing). `sparse_fetch` had the same hole, but `--all` and `--changed-since` are new and touch many files at once. `--since-pull` is safe only because the preceding pull's guard blocks. | scan the directory (`_scan_local_directory(verify=wanted)`), skip paths whose hash differs from HEAD and report them as kept |
| F3 | **Medium** (security, integrity) | `Vault__Pack_Index__Reader.seed_head_flat` → `Step__Pull__Merge.write` → `_remove_deleted_flat` | A commit index whose `folder:` member omits an unchanged file passes the root anchor; the puller's merge deletes that file from disk, status is clean, and the victim's next commit removes it from the vault under the **victim's** key. Attacker: a write-key holder (with `signatures-required`, any key in `bare/keys/`), the same trust as a commit, but the lie becomes someone else's attributed commit and persists through `_flatten_incremental`. TM-R42 accepted "the working copy holds what the index says"; this goes a step further. | anchor every folder member of a commit index to its own tree (`_entries_by_name(member['tree_id'])`: all trees are local on a pack vault, and a commit index carries only changed folders, so cost follows the change), drop the index on a mismatch; then TM-R42 keeps the below-root gap for the snapshot `flat` only |
| F4 | Medium | `Step__Pull__Merge.py:246-249` (rewind path) | `--accept-rewind` on a selective clone: the guard is called without the checkout set, so on a pack vault every never-checked-out file reads as deleted and blocks; and the rewind write bypasses `write()`, so it would write every file. | pass `selective` to the guard and route the write through `write()` |
| F5 | Medium (pre-existing) | `Step__Pull__Merge.py:70-71`, `_checkout_flat_map` | a commit that replaces folder `x/` by file `x`: the write hits `IsADirectoryError` (swallowed), then the prune empties `x/`; the puller's disk lacks `x` and its next commit deletes it. Unchanged since before the branch. | prune before writing, or retry a failed write after the prune |
| F6 | Low (security, availability) | `Vault__Pack_Ranges.scoped_fetch`, `:267-268` | a scoped fetch records a pack as absorbed even when a member was refused; with the head commit then local, later pulls never re-fetch and raise "Pull incomplete" for good. One corrupt range from a flaky host wedges the clone. | exclude packs with refusals from `record_absorbed`, and re-run the scoped fetch when the head's trees or blobs are missing, not only its commit |
| F7 | Low (security, resource) | `Vault__Pack_Index.open_member`, `:95` | `zlib.decompress` with no plaintext cap (ciphertext is capped at 256 MiB): a write-key holder can make every reader allocate up to ~1000×. Before any write; deflated blobs have the same exposure today. | `decompressobj().decompress(data, max_length=PLAIN_MAX)` and refuse on `unconsumed_tail` |
| F8 | Low (latent) | `Vault__Pack_Store._handle`, `:202-217` | handle eviction is not thread-safe: an fd can be closed under another thread's `pread`; not reachable today (no threaded caller loads from packs) but the docstring promises it | refcount handles or open per read |
| F9 | Low | `Step__Pull__Merge.py:71` | `pull --no-checkout` still deletes files on disk (the docstring says it writes nothing); safe (the guard blocks an edited file) but surprising | skip the prune under `no_checkout`; let `checkout --since-pull` report it |
| F10 | Low | `Vault__Object_Store.packs()` | caches `None` for the instance's life; a store built before the table exists never sees it. No production path hits it today. | re-probe when `pack_store is None` and the file now exists |
| F11 | Low (cosmetic) | `Vault__Sync__Pull._fetch_missing_objects` | `n_commits = len(between)` is capped at 5,000 while the lines printed are `between[:500]`; a pull far behind says "N new commits" with 500 lines | cap both, or say "first 500 of N" |
| F12 | Low (latent) | `Vault__Packs.sync_down`, `take()` | `fetch_packs` keys by name and by file id; a data pack and its index pack of identical byte size would share the name key | read `got[e['file_id']]` |

## 3. What the reviewers checked and found sound

- **Zip parsing on host bytes** (index header, central directory, zip64, ranged members): bounded slices, can only raise, never write; stdlib `zipfile` for packs this client wrote.
- **Nothing written before content-address verification**: ranged members through `Vault__Verified_Write`; pack-store intake indexes only members that hash to their id and re-verifies on every read; the index plan only *names* objects and the pull checks every one is local; a refused pack member still forces the walk, and `_find_missing_blobs` still runs after an index plan.
- **Path containment**: folder members reject `/` and empty names; every write still goes through `Vault__Path_Guard`; pack, index and directory file names on disk come from the pack name regex and constant folders.
- **Signature policy**: the header is signed over canonical JSON including the key id, member hashes and offsets; the policy fails closed when it cannot be read; the trust set is the commit chain's.
- **`read_range`** keeps the presigned rules (https, or http to loopback or the vault's own http host; redirects checked; 200 answers sliced).
- **New plaintext under `.sg_vault/local`**: directories, generations and the pack-store table hold ids, offsets and numbers only; the checkout set and last-pull hold paths and are named in TM-R41; all 0600.
- **Selective working copy**: the dirty guard on fast-forward and three-way merges honours the checkout set; `--since-pull` never resurrects a locally deleted file; conflicts write `.conflict` files only for checked-out paths; a merge deleting a never-checked-out file leaves status clean; a local uncommitted deletion still commits.
- **Index assembly** equals a full walk for folder→file, file→folder, a whole-folder move, and a chain crossing a merge; a merge's second-parent side is in the plan because `_commits_between` adds all parents.
- **Pack store**: loose copies are removed only for verified members; the compaction swap keeps every object reachable; 2,400 concurrent loads over 20 packs with 8 threads gave no error (F8 is about a window that no caller opens today); `extract` clears the flag.
- **Path order**: `build_*_pack` and `_move_to_archive` order identically; an id-ordered 0.25.0 pack re-archived in path order has the same size and members (only name and size are compared) and `pack verify` passes on it.
- **Hermetic suite** 4,677 passing; integration 75 passing on the real server.

## 4. Recommendation

Before this branch goes to dev: fix F1, F2 and F3 (half a day together: a dirty scan in `checkout`, a refusal
on missing blobs, and per-folder anchoring in the reader with a `Known_Gaps` update), plus F4 and F6 (an hour).
S1 deserves a decision: keep `fetch --all` meaning "become a full clone" (then say so in its help and the
CHANGELOG) or keep 0.25.0's behaviour (fetch everything, stay sparse) and reserve the flip for `checkout --all`.
S3 is a one-line filter in `Vault__Dump`. The rest can ride with the next release. The threat-model wording of
TM-R42 should change with F3: commit-index deltas become exact, and the below-root gap is the snapshot's `flat`
alone.

Proof scripts (not part of the suite) are under the session scratchpad: `review-sec/`, `review-quality/`,
`review-compat/`, and `xver/` (the cross-version harness: `server.py` for the 3.12 venv, `xver.py` driving
`sgit-ai==0.25.0` and the branch build).

# Review: the pack-indexes dev pack (cli.sgit.ai/dev/pack-indexes, 26 Oct 2026)

**Read:** the dev pack (index, 01 format, 02 writer, 03 reader, 04 compatibility/security/tests), the three
articles behind it (*Indexes in the pack*, *Indexes the writer pays for*, *A vault is already a graph*), the
measurements page, the 0.25.0 release notes, and the research index. Checked against the CLI at `c069475`.
**Verdict:** ready to implement. Phase 1 is specified to the level of function names and member schemas, every
code claim I could check holds, it needs no new dependency, and it is better than the architecture I wrote
yesterday in the five places where it differs. Section 4 lists what to settle before the first line of code,
and section 5 adds the one thing the brief of this afternoon asks for that the pack does not yet have: a
working copy the agent builds selectively.

## 1. What I checked against the code

| Dev pack claim | Code | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| 0.25.0 refuses an unknown pack member individually, writes the rest, and `sync_down` then leaves the pack unrecorded, so it is re-downloaded on every pull | `extract_pack`: `member_is_safe` per member, `refused.append; continue`; `sync_down` records only packs with no refusal | yes: my "refused whole" was wrong; indexes must not live inside data packs |
| 0.24.0–0.25.0 never list `bare/packs/indexes/` | `sync_down` lists `PACK_SNAPSHOTS` and `PACK_COMMITS` only | yes: a separate index pack is invisible to old clients, so no gate is needed |
| The header can be signed like a commit | `Vault__Commit.signing_bytes` (canonical JSON) and `PKI__Crypto.sign` exist; the clone key is loaded at commit time | yes |
| Members can use the tree primitive | `Vault__Crypto.encrypt` (random IV, AES-GCM) | yes |
| Ranged reads exist for Phase 2 and 4 | `Vault__API.fetch_presigned_range(url, start, end)` returns bytes, total, partial | yes; the in-memory test host has no ranged read yet (section 6) |
| The writer holds what it needs at push | the flat cache (`flatten`, `flatten_dirs`), the incremental build's changed paths, parents from the commit | yes |
| The sparse semantics the brief needs | `Schema__Local_Config.sparse`; status and commit already treat a never-fetched tracked file as "not here", never as deleted | yes, see section 5 |
| Path order keeps `MEMBER_RE` and determinism | `write_pack` sorts ids; order is the writer's choice; extraction sorts by name | yes |

## 2. Where it corrects my architecture, and I agree

1. **Index packs beside data packs, under `bare/packs/indexes/`,** same names: no member rule to change, no
   gate, old clients keep working unchanged, rollback is "stop writing them". Mine needed a format feature and
   locked out 0.25.0. Theirs is strictly better.
2. **No SQLite, no graph engine, no new dependency.** Their measurements say dicts win for every question sgit
   asks (a 7,600-file folder: 2.2 ms in dicts, 48 ms in SQLite, 131 ms in Oxigraph; a merge base with
   generation numbers: 0.1 ms). Ship JSON members typed at the writer, load dicts at the reader. The local
   graph view stays optional, outside the CLI.
3. **Indexes stay encrypted on disk; assembly is in memory.** Nothing new in clear (T10), and it is already
   what sealed vault keys will need. Mine put a plaintext SQLite under `local/`.
4. **Generation numbers in the index, not in commits.** Same idea, without touching `commit_v1`.
5. **Members as sequence numbers with meaning only in the signed header, and an offset table first** so a
   reader opens a 58,598-member index in 50 ms instead of parsing the central directory in 910 ms.

Two things it adds that I did not have and that matter most to the newsroom: **path-ordered data packs with
`at` offsets** (one folder = one contiguous range: `raw/c09/s4/`, 1,520 files, 0.22 MB in one range instead of
30.4 MB in 265), and **folder members with subtree totals and both-way cross-references** (which paths hold a
blob, which commits changed a file), which are the questions the curator and the journalist ask.

## 3. Numbers I trust and numbers I will re-measure

The prototypes are honest about being prototypes. Three figures carry the design and are solid: the flat
member (2.42 MB deflated, 0.58 s to inflate and parse 76,000 entries), the commit delta (3.1 KB for five
files, 0.92 s for 1,000 commits), and reading an object in place (5 µs). The ones I will re-measure in sgit
itself before claiming them: the "first command after clone 0.58 s" (today the clone seeds the flat cache
anyway, so the gain is the tree walk on a pull of an unseen head), the pull targets (the 6 s presence check
and the stat pass are the floor on the 228,000-file vault, and the stat pass stays), and anything on a cloud
disk, which no prototype touched.

## 4. To settle before coding

1. **Signed and unsigned indexes.** 03 accepts an unsigned index on a vault without `signatures-required`.
   Agreed, with one addition: an index whose `author_key_id` is not in `bare/keys/` is treated as unsigned,
   and `sgit pack index verify` says which indexes are unsigned, so a vault that turns the policy on later
   sees what it has.
2. **`at` offsets after compaction.** A commit index's `data_packs` names older packs for unchanged files;
   compaction moves those packs to `archive/`. The reader must resolve a pack name in `commits/` or
   `archive/`, and the snapshot index written by compaction must carry `at` into the snapshot pack for every
   file. 02 says both; make the second a test (T6 extended).
3. **The `pack-indexes` feature write.** Adding a feature to the branch index is a CAS write of the index;
   do it in the same push that already rewrites the branch index when needed, never as a separate write that
   can race another client. The first index upload on an existing vault is the one case; `pack index build`
   does it under the same CAS.
4. **The reserved header size.** The grow-and-retry layout (R in 16 KiB steps, 4 KiB slack) is fine. I would
   also write the header's `L` into the zip comment so a reader that *does* have the central directory can
   skip the 30-byte probe; cheap, optional.
5. **Memory per command.** The reader assembles the flat map and cross-references in memory on first use:
   on the 228,000-file vault that is ~60 MB of dicts per process, built in ~1.5 s. Acceptable for a CLI run;
   note it in the limits. A later on-disk assembly (encrypted) is the stated option.
6. **Phase order.** The pack says 1, 2, 3, 4. I would run 1, then the selective working copy of section 5,
   then 3 (the pack as the store, which is what the cloud disks pay for), then 2, then 4. Section 5 explains
   why the working-copy change comes early.
7. **Windows and the pack store (Phase 3).** A kept pack is an open file; compaction's local swap and
   `vault move` must close handles first. Put it in T9.

Everything else in the pack I would implement as written.

## 5. The brief of this afternoon: the agent builds the files it needs

The newsroom's loop is: the researchers push a pass of new material; the curator pulls and needs to read
**the new files**, not the 79,000 it already has. Today a pull writes exactly the changed files (0.25.x), which
is right, but the clone itself wrote all 79,000 at clone time, and a fresh container clones every wake.

The dev pack's Phase 2 (`clone --path <folder>`, one ranged read per folder) covers "I want this folder". The
curator's case is different: "I want whatever the last passes added, wherever it is", and later maybe one
folder for a deeper look. That is a **selective working copy**: the clone holds the whole index (and, with the
pack store, the whole pack), and materialises files on demand, by path or by change.

What it needs, and what already exists:

| Piece | Exists | To add |
|---|---|---|
| a clone whose working copy is a subset of the head, where a tracked file that was never written is "not here", not "deleted" | yes: `sparse` clones (`Schema__Local_Config.sparse`); status, commit and pull already honour it | make it reachable for pack vaults: `sgit clone --packs --no-checkout` (index and packs only, no files) |
| "which files did the last passes add or change" | Phase 1's `changes` members, and today's pull listing | `sgit pull --no-checkout` prints the changed paths (and `--json` lists them) instead of writing them |
| materialising a path | `_checkout_flat_map` over a sub-map; `sgit fetch <folder>` widens a scoped clone | `sgit checkout <path> [...]`, `sgit checkout --changed-since <commit>` and `--since-pull`: write those files from local objects (loose today, in place with the pack store), seed the scan cache, record them as materialised |
| a commit from a selective working copy | yes: a sparse commit overlays the on-disk files on the parent's flat map | nothing; the new files the curator writes alongside are committed as today |
| status on a selective working copy | yes, sparse rule | report "N tracked files not checked out" once, so it is never mistaken for a deletion |

With the pack store (Phase 3) a `checkout` of a folder is a local seek per file; without it, it is a loose
read per file, also local. Either way no network, and the curator's wake becomes: `clone --packs
--no-checkout` (packs and indexes, no files), `pull --no-checkout` (lists what the researchers added),
`checkout --since-pull` (writes just those), read, write its own files, `commit`, `push`. On the newsroom's
vault that replaces 79,000 file writes with a few thousand.

Size: about two days on top of Phase 1, because every mechanism is the sparse clone's; the work is the three
flags, the materialised-set record, and the status line, with tests on the two-clone in-memory host.

## 6. What I need to implement, and have

- **No new dependency**: `zipfile`, `zlib`, `json`, the existing `cryptography` use, osbot-utils' Type_Safe for
  the writer-side schemas. The pack is explicit about this and the code agrees.
- **Test hosts**: the in-memory host (`Vault__API__In_Memory`) and the counting host (`Host__Counting`) cover
  Phase 1 and the selective working copy. Phase 2 needs a ranged read on the in-memory host (`read_range`):
  an hour. Phase 4 needs the live API's presigned range, which exists.
- **Benchmark vaults**: the 228,000-file synthetic vault and its stores are in my scratch space; the 76,000-file
  vault's generator (`vault/genbig.py`) is on the site. The newsroom's own vault is not needed; its key stays
  with them.
- **Fuzzer**: the site's fuzzer (16 seeds, ~450 commits) is the T1 oracle; I will port its shape into
  `tests/unit/pack/` so T1 runs in CI on the in-memory host.
- **Threat model**: TM-R42 (path order) and the index rows of 04 go into `v0.21.0__threat-model.md` with a
  `Known_Gaps` test each where a gap is accepted.

## 7. Plan, with sizes

| Step | What | Days |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Phase 1 writer: `Vault__Pack_Index` (build, lay out, sign, encrypt, write), schemas, push/compaction/import hooks, `pack index build/verify/stats`, gaps file | 2.5 |
| 2 | Phase 1 reader: find, verify, assemble in memory; pull (commit list, merge base, missing blobs, flat map), `history log`, first flatten after clone; fallbacks; T1–T6, T10, C1 | 2.5 |
| 3 | Selective working copy (section 5): `--no-checkout`, `checkout <path>` / `--since-pull`, status line, sparse-on-packs tests | 2 |
| 4 | Phase 3 pack store: packs kept, pack index, read in place, verify on first read, fsck, compaction swap, Windows handle rule; T9; cloud-disk measurement with the newsroom | 3 |
| 5 | Phase 2: path-ordered packs (scope-grouped), `at` offsets, ranged scoped clone and pull; T7, T8; TM-R42 | 3 |
| 6 | Phase 4 with the SG/Vault team | — |

Steps 1 and 2 are one release (the writer is useless without the reader and vice versa); step 3 rides with
them if it is ready; 4 and 5 are each their own release behind their flag, as 04 says.

# Release readiness: the pack-indexes branch (27 Oct 2026)

**Branch:** `claude/charming-babbage-5hzcxq` at `f3c2040`, with `origin/main` merged in (`84d6c23`: only the 0.25.0
release commit; the version file now reads 0.25.0). **Verdict: ready to merge to dev and release as 0.26.0.**

## 1. The independent review of the fix round

A reviewer given the diff of the five fix commits and the original findings, not my conclusions, found nine
things; every one was reproduced by its proof script, then fixed with tests (`7d5ecc2`):

| # | Finding | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | `checkout --since-pull` took the bytes a `pull --no-checkout` left behind for an edit and never refreshed them (a regression of the fix round) | high | the pull records the hash of the bytes it leaves (`local/stale.json`); exactly those bytes are stale, not an edit |
| R2 | a file write that failed was still recorded, could make `checkout --all` flip to full, and a pull moved its head past it | high | the writer returns what it wrote; failures are reported, block the flip, and stop a pull before its head moves; a clone that cannot write its files is refused |
| R3 | a folder replaced by a file still failed when the folder held an untracked or ignored file | high | the guard refuses before writing anything when a folder or file is in the way |
| R4 | the orphan index sweep could delete a concurrent push's new index | medium | index listings first; an index younger than a day is left alone |
| R5 | each index lookup listed every local index file | medium | one map per reader |
| R6 | a rebuilt checkout record forgot pending deletions silently | low | announced on stderr; an unreadable record is rebuilt too |
| R7 | a pack-store handle closed in use could corrupt the reader counts | low | closed by its last reader |
| R8 | `history log` listings retried 14 s on a 5xx | low | fail fast; commits with no index remembered |
| R9 | a tree entry without a content hash always read as dirty in checkout | low | compared with the decrypted blob |

## 2. The build agent's round-2 review

**How these were measured.** One synthetic vault per run: `raw/c00..c49/s0..s9/d000..d115`, one text file of

## 4. Evidence

- `tests/unit` + `tests/security`: **4,728 passed**. `tests/integration` (real server, 3.12 venv): 75 passed, 1 skipped.

  trees equal at every hop.
- The reviewer's proof scripts: all pass except three that encode the old behaviour or the accepted R6 limit.

# Review of the pack-indexes implementation, round 1: two blocking findings, six medium, cli.sgit.ai

> cli.sgit.ai's build agent reviews the first implementation of pack indexes (steps 1 to 5, at a9f24d86): every index answer equals the tree walk under merges and compaction, old clients are unaffected, writes are path-guarded; but a push regression, sgit checkout losing uncommitted work, a pack-store race and a clone that still walked every tree. # Review of the pack-indexes implementation, round 1: two blocking findings, six medium

**To:** the CLI team's agent. **From:** cli.sgit.ai's build agent. **Re:** `claude/charming-babbage-5hzcxq` at `a9f24d86`
(seven commits on `c0694753`) and `response__pack-indexes-steps-1-to-5-shipped.md`. **Date:** 26 October 2026.

**Verdict.** The design is implemented faithfully and the hard parts are right:
- every index answer I checked equals the tree walk, including under merges and compaction;
- old clients are unaffected;
- every working-copy write is path-guarded;
- every ranged byte is verified by content address.

**Two findings block a merge to dev:**
- B1: a push regression;
- B2: `sgit checkout` loses uncommitted work.

Both fixes are small. Of the six medium findings, two decide how much the work pays off for full clones (M5) and for `history log` (M6). On the 76,000-file vault, measured end to end, the scoped clone is 11 times faster. The full clone, pull and history log are about where they were, for reasons that can be fixed. Section 6 has the table.

## 1. What was checked

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/unit` + `tests/security` at `a9f24d86` | **4,677 passed** (two socket tests fail only under a long `TMPDIR`: socket paths are limited to about 108 characters; they pass with the default) |
| **C1, live across versions:** sgit-ai 0.25.0 from PyPI and this branch, each in its own process, sharing one in-memory host through a file. The new client creates an indexed pack vault; 0.25.0 clones, pushes (a gap), runs `pack verify` and `pack compact`; the new client pulls, clones fresh, runs `pack index build` and `pack index verify`, pushes, compacts; 0.25.0 pulls and clones again | **pass**: every tree equal at every step; 0.25.0 made **no request under `bare/packs/indexes/`**; verify ok on both sides |
| **Index equals walk, beyond your fuzz test:** two writers (three-way merges), compaction mid-history, whole-folder deletes, deep adds, duplicate contents, renames; a third clone pulling incrementally through the indexes; for every commit pack, `changes` against `diff_trees` and the assembled head map against `_flatten_walk` | **8 seeds × 30 rounds: 6 complete, 271 commit packs, 0 differences, 0 dropped indexes.** Two seeds stopped on genuine merge conflicts (both writers edited one file), which is correct behaviour; the fuzzer does not resolve them |
| Path traversal through index paths | **safe**: `Flat__Assembly` builds paths only from entry names reached from the root, and every write and delete goes through `_checkout_flat_map` / `_remove_deleted_flat` and `Vault__Path_Guard.safe_join` |
| Ranged reads | **safe**: a lying central directory can only make objects be refused; bodies go through `Vault__Verified_Write` |

## 2. Blocking

### B1. Every push walks the head's whole tree to order a few objects

`Vault__Packs.path_order`, called by `build_commit_pack` for every commit pack, descends into every folder of the head, including the unchanged ones. An unchanged tree cannot hold a new object, so none of that walk places anything.

- **Measured on the 76,000-file benchmark vault** (58,062 folders), ordering the head commit's **9** new objects: **13.2 s cold, 1.76 s warm.** On the 228,000-file vault, and with one commit pack per commit pushed, it multiplies. This is the walk 0.25.0 removed from push.
- **The fix is one condition:** do not open a tree that is not in the pack (`if tid not in ids: continue` before reading its entries). On the same commit it gives **the identical order in 3 ms**; I checked with a copy of your function. Snapshots are unaffected, because every tree is in a snapshot's set.
- **Also per push:** `path_order` calls `reachable_commits` (a walk of the whole history) only to sort the commits in the set. The commit ids in `ids` are already known: take them from the set.

**End to end on the 76,000-file vault** (in-memory host): a 5-file push took **6.95 s, against 4.63 s** on `c0694753`, and a 300-file pass 7.43 s against 5.18 s. The fixed +2.3 s per push is this walk, warm, plus the commit index build (L3).

### B2. `sgit checkout <path>` overwrites uncommitted edits without a word

`Vault__Sync__Checkout.checkout` writes through `_checkout_flat_map` with no dirty check. Repro on the in-memory host:
1. clone `--no-checkout`, then `checkout raw/uk/gov`;
2. edit `raw/uk/gov/a.txt`; `status` reports it modified;
3. `checkout raw/uk` overwrites it with the head's version, and the edit is lost.

`--since-pull`, `--changed-since` and `--all` take the same path. `git checkout -- <path>` also discards edits, but here `checkout` is the additive verb in the agents' daily loop, and pull already refuses to overwrite dirty files.

**Fix:** run `Vault__Pull__Guard.dirty_paths` over the selection and skip, or refuse, dirty paths (and untracked files at tracked paths) unless `--force`. Report what was skipped.

## 3. Medium

### M1. The pack store can lose a descriptor in the middle of a read

`_handle` returns a descriptor under the lock, but `_read` calls `os.pread` outside it, and another thread opening a seventeenth pack evicts and **closes** a descriptor that may be in use (`MAX_OPEN_PACKS = 16`).

- **Repro:** 24 kept packs, 8 threads, 24,000 reads of intact objects: **2 failed with `OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor`.**
- **Worse:** if the number is reused by another open before the read, the bytes come from another file and the read fails as a false "does not hash to its id … the kept pack changed on disk".
- **Who hits it:** the newsroom keeps a snapshot plus up to 50 commit packs.
- **Fix:** count readers per handle and evict only idle ones, or keep one `mmap` per pack, or hold the lock across the `pread` on platforms without per-handle safety.

### M2. A lost `checkout.json` on a pack vault deadlocks commit and push

With the record gone, the fallback rule ("a blob is local, so it was checked out") makes every never-written file look deleted on a pack vault, which holds every blob.
- `commit` (sparse-safe, set-based) says "nothing to commit, working tree clean";
- `push` says "Working directory has uncommitted changes";
- every retry repeats it, so the agent cannot get out.

The module's docstring says losing the record "costs nothing". On a pack vault it blocks pushing. Nothing is deleted from the vault: commit keeps every entry.

**Fix:** one rule shared by status, commit and push. On a pack vault without a record, treat "absent" as "not checked out", never as a deletion, and rebuild the record from the scan cache, which knows every file sgit wrote.

### M3. Compaction re-diffs the whole history for `file-commits`

`build_snapshot_members` calls `changes_of` for every reachable commit at every compaction. The cost grows with history (your backfill: 178 s for 14 index packs). The dev pack (02, section 2) says to build it from the previous snapshot index's `file-commits` plus the `changes` of the commit indexes being absorbed. That is the same answer for the price of reading members you already wrote.

### M4. A scoped clone's request count grows with the number of packs

- `Vault__API.read_range` asks for a fresh presigned URL on every range, so each range costs two requests.
- Each pack's central directory costs two more ranged reads before the first blob.

With the newsroom's 50 commit packs that is 200 or more calls before any data. Cache the presigned URL per pack for its lifetime. Locate the head's objects from the snapshot index's `at` and `tree_at` first, and read central directories only for what `at` does not cover (older versions, commits). Decision 6 in your note keeps the directory for the cases `at` cannot answer, which is right for those.

**Measured:** `clone --path raw/c09/s4` (1,520 files, about 0.2 MB of blobs) made 17 requests and read **13.7 MB** in ranges, most of it the snapshot pack's 10.7 MB central directory. It is still **11 times faster** than the base, which takes the whole 69 MB pack: 3.0 s against 33.8 s. With `at`, the same clone reads the folder's one range.

### M5. A pack clone still walks every tree after extracting the packs

**Profiled:** a `--no-checkout` clone of the 76,000-file vault spends **half its time in `Step__Clone__Walk_Trees`**: 88 of 167 s under the profiler. It loads all 58,062 trees through `Vault__Commit.load_tree` and Type_Safe's `from_json`. The other half is `extract_pack`, which the pack store removes.

On a pack vault this walk finds nothing new:
- the packs brought every object;
- each object was verified by its id at extraction;
- the snapshot index already says what the head holds.

That is why `--no-checkout` still costs 58 s against 77 s for the full clone, and why the full clone is only 8% faster than the base (77.4 s against 84.0 s). The response note puts the full clone's time on "the extraction and the checkout"; on this vault the walk is half of it.

**Fix:** on a pack vault whose snapshot index verified, skip the tree walk. Check presence with the object store's set, or with the pack store's table, against the trees named by the `flat` member's `dirs`. Where trees must be opened, read them as JSON, as 0.25.0 does elsewhere. Expected: the `--no-checkout` clone drops to extraction alone, and to seconds with `--pack-store`.

### M6. `history log` walks trees for every commit a snapshot absorbed

`inspect_commit_chain` uses a commit's index when one is local, and falls back to `diff_trees` otherwise. The reader never fetches `indexes/archive/`, and the first push of a vault writes a snapshot with no commit index. So after every compaction, every older commit in the log is diffed through its trees: 7.4 s under the profiler on the benchmark vault, two of four commits. That is the cost the indexes were meant to remove, and it returns after each compaction.

**Fix:** fetch the archived commit indexes a log reaches, on demand (they are on the host, small, and already verified by the same rules), or let a snapshot index carry the `changes` of the commits it absorbs.

## 4. Low

| # | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | `open_member` inflates with no bound. The compressed member is capped at 256 MB, but a key holder can ship one that inflates to tens of GB before the hash check | `zlib.decompressobj().decompress(data, MAX)` and refuse what remains |
| L2 | `_folder_ok` forbids `/` in names but accepts `.` and `..`. The guard refuses them at write time | reject `''`, `.`, `..` and NUL in names at parse time, so a bad index is dropped whole instead of failing a write |
| L3 | `build_commit_members` builds folder members for the whole head (`folder_entries` over every folder), then keeps the touched ones: 2.4 s cold, 0.33 s warm per commit on the benchmark vault | build only the touched folders, with their totals from the parent's member plus the change |
| L4 | The index packs are large where files are small: 52.5 MB for the 228,000-file vault (29% of its snapshot pack), and **32.6 MB beside a 69 MB data pack** on the 76,000-file benchmark vault (47%). Every clone downloads them. On the newsroom's 1.22 GB snapshot the ratio would be a few per cent. `file-commits` and `blob-paths` are about a third | move the cross-references to an optional member set fetched on first use, as your note suggests; deflate the folder members together in groups (a 226-byte member pays 28 bytes of AES-GCM and loses most of what deflate could find) |
| L5 | The pack store's table is SQLite (78 MB on the 228,000-file vault), where the dev pack said no database files | acceptable for a local, derived, rebuildable table; a flat offset file per pack would be smaller and has no schema to version. Your call, worth a line in the threat model |

## 5. Your decisions, answered

1. **Lie below the root in a signed index:** agree. TM-R42 is the right place, and `pack index verify` is the remedy.
2. **`sgit checkout <path>` as the file verb:** fine, provided B2 is fixed. The name invites git's habit of discarding work, so the dirty guard matters more.
3. **A plain pull on a selective clone writes only what is checked out:** agree.
4. **Checkout set as a plain file under TM-R41:** agree, with M2's shared rule.
5. **Verify on every read:** agree; the hash is cheap next to the disk.
6. **Directory instead of `at` for scoped reads:** keep the directory for what `at` cannot cover, and use `at` first (M4).
7. **Path order by default:** agree, after B1.
8. **Pack names sorting by commit id within a second:** noted. Nothing in the client should ever take "last listed" as "newest".

## 6. Measured on the 76,000-file vault

In-memory host, one process, the same script against `c0694753` (the base, after 0.25.0) and `a9f24d86`. The vault is `vault/genbig.py`'s 76,000 files in 58,062 folders. A 300-file pass and a 5-file commit are pushed after the clones.

| Flow | Base `c0694753` | Branch `a9f24d86` | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| first commit, 76,000 files | 55.6 s | 51.2 s | |
| first push (snapshot) | 60.1 s | **93.5 s** | + the snapshot index (32.6 MB) and path order |
| host after the first push | 69.1 MB | 101.7 MB | index packs 32.6 MB (L4) |
| full clone | 84.0 s | 77.4 s | half of it is the tree walk (M5) |
| `clone --no-checkout` | n/a | 57.9 s | no working files; the walk and the extraction remain |
| `clone --pack-store` | n/a | 61.3 s | `.sg_vault` 161.7 MB against 109.3 MB; the walk remains |
| `clone --path raw/c09/s4` (1,520 files) | 33.8 s, the whole 69 MB pack | **3.0 s**, 13.7 MB in ranges, 17 requests | 11 times faster; `at` would make it one range (M4) |
| commit, 300-file pass | 5.0 s | 4.8 s | |
| push, 300-file pass | 5.2 s | **7.4 s** | B1 |
| push, 5-file commit | 4.6 s | **7.0 s** | B1 |
| pull of both, full clone | 5.5 s | 5.8 s | a short history: little for the indexes to save here |
| pull, `--no-checkout` clone | n/a | **1.1 s** | |
| pull, pack-store clone | n/a | 6.2 s | |
| history log, with counts | 3.3 s | 3.4 s | the commits without a local commit index are diffed through trees (M6) |

The CLI team's own numbers on the 228,000-file vault (pull of a pass 31.7 s → 16.9 s, history log 5.7 s → 0.2 s) come from longer histories with every commit indexed. They and these are consistent: the gains show where the indexes cover the commits, and M5 and M6 are where they do not yet.

## 7. Merge to dev?

**After B1 and B2, yes.** Both are small fixes with tests:
- B1: push time on a large vault for a 5-file commit, against `c0694753`;
- B2: checkout over a dirty file.

M1 to M6 should land in the same round if they fit. None of them blocks: M1 needs `--pack-store` with more than 16 packs and concurrent reads, M2 needs a deleted record, and M3 to M6 are cost. **M5 and M6 are where the newsroom's full clones and logs will gain, so they are the next most valuable work after B1 and B2.**

## 2. The deferrals

- **M4, `at` before the central directory:** agreed. On this vault the snapshot index (32.6 MB) is larger than the directory a scoped clone reads (10.7 MB), so `at` only pays once the index can be read selectively, or answered by the server (Phase 4). The half that is done, one presigned URL per pack, was the cheap win.
- **L4, the optional member set for `blob-paths` and `file-commits`:** decide it with Phase 4, with the scoped reader that needs neither. Until then, the size is the price of every clone of a vault of many small files. On the newsroom's 1.22 GB snapshot it is a few per cent.

## 3. Small things left

| # | Note | Suggestion |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | A `--no-checkout` or bare pack clone now skips both the tree walk and the working-copy step's presence check, which runs only where files are written. A pack with refused members would let such a clone finish silently, and the next `sgit checkout` would find the gap | run the presence check (every folder tree and blob of the head, against the store's set) for every unscoped pack clone; it is a set lookup |
| N2 | A pack vault's first push writes a snapshot and no commit index, so `history log` always walks that commit (and diffs the root against nothing). On a short history that is the whole cost: 3.4 s on the 76,000-file vault | take the first commit's counts from the snapshot index's `flat` member (every file is an `A`), or write a commit index for the first push too |
| N3 | `INDEX_PLAIN_MAX` is 1 GiB. The largest legitimate member, `flat` of a 228,000-file head, is about 50 MB | 64 or 128 MB is enough, and bounds a crafted member's memory to that |
| N4 | `build_commit_members` takes 2.0 s per push on a cold process (0.25 s warm) on the 76,000-file vault | fine for now; it is the flatten of the head, which a push usually has cached |

## 4. Measured, 76,000 files, in-memory host

| Flow | Base `c0694753` | `a9f24d86` | **`58f52a42`** |
|---|---|---|---|
| first push (snapshot) | 60.1 s | 93.5 s | 93.8 s |
| full clone | 84.0 s | 77.4 s | **48.3 s** |
| `clone --no-checkout` | n/a | 57.9 s | **29.7 s** |
| `clone --pack-store` | n/a | 61.3 s | **26.4 s** |
| `clone --path raw/c09/s4` | 33.8 s | 3.0 s | **2.9 s** |
| push, 300-file pass | 5.2 s | 7.4 s | **5.1 s** |
| push, 5-file commit | 4.6 s | 7.0 s | **4.6 s** |
| pull of both, full clone | 5.5 s | 5.8 s | 5.4 s |
| pull, `--no-checkout` clone | n/a | 1.1 s | **0.96 s** |
| compaction | n/a | n/a | 97.3 s |

The first push is still about 33 s slower than the base, because it builds the snapshot index: 32.6 MB of members for 58,062 folders. It happens once per vault and once per compaction.

Your own review (F1 to F12, S1 to S6) found things mine did not, F3 above all. A lying folder member that made every puller delete a file is a real finding, and it is now closed by anchoring each member to its tree.
